Big Bend Conservation Area – Camping
Camping in Big Bend Conservation Area is available for nightly, weekly, or seasonal rates from Victoria Day weekend until Thanksgiving Day.
See activities
Book a campsite

Big Bend Conservation Area
21239 Big Bend Rd
Southwest Middlesex, ON
N0L 2P0
General Inquiries
For day-use visitors, a
rentable pavilion
is available in the designated area—ideal for group gatherings and special events.
Big Bend Conservation Area
21239 Big Bend Rd
Southwest Middlesex, ON
N0L 2P0

Camping Rules


p
Camping Information
Big Bend offers a total of
48 campsites , including:
4 sites with 30-amp electrical service and water
2 sites with 15-amp electrical service and water
2 group camping sites
10 riverfront sites offering a more natural, backcountry-style experience
30 unserviced sites for traditional camping
Seasonal sites (to be placed on the waitlist please click the GENERAL INQUIRIES button)
A
serviced washroom building with showers is available from Victoria Day Weekend through mid-October.
Please note that there is no dumping station on site.
Camping reservations open for the upcoming season March 1 of the same year.
First-come, first-served sites
are available for campers who have not reserved online. Camping fees are collected regularly.

Camping
Conservation area camping in Southern Ontario
Campgrounds near London and Chatham located within Lower Thames Valley Conservation Authority
See our campgrounds
4 Campgrounds for you to Pick and Choose your Camping Adventure!
The Lower Thames Valley Conservation Authority has 4 conservation areas with camping.
Whether you’re wanting to organize group camping or get out by yourself, you can bring your tent if you’re in the mood for some off-the-grid adventures or pull your trailer into one of our fully serviced spots so you have all the amenities of home.
C.M Wilson Conservation Area and Big Bend Conservation Area have traditional campgrounds, book a site and bring your RV or tent!
If you don’t own a camping shelter you can book cabins at E.M Warwick Conservation Area!
If you have a community group that loves to camp check out our group camping at Longwoods Road, C.M Wilson, E.M Warwick, Big Bend Conservation Areas!
Every campground and conservation area is different, why not explore them all?

Seasonal Island Camping Lottery
Seasonal Island Camping Lottery
Brockville offers camping in St. Lawrence Park Campground, and on certain City of Brockville Islands.
The 2026 camping season is open on May 15th, with bookings starting via our online campsite reservation system on May 1st for St. Lawrence Park, directly below and City of Brockville Islands .
St. Lawrence Park
For those travelers to Brockville who enjoy camping, one of the City’s most attractive waterfront park areas is St. Lawrence Park (525 King Street West) located on the western edge of the City on County Road 2.
The park includes camping facilities which operate from Victoria Day weekend to Labour Day offering fully serviced (15 amp electrical outlet and water) and non-serviced sites. Sewage hookup is not available, however, a dump station is on site for registered campers.
The park has a beautiful safe sandy beach ideal for children which is supervised during the summer period. Washrooms, change rooms, and a canteen are in operation from June through to September. A canoe and kayak launching area is available at the western edge of the park.
Day use at the park is free; however, charges do apply for overnight camping. Please see the camping rate below for current rates. St. Lawrence Park welcomes cyclists and has an “always room” policy for self-supported cyclists.
During the camping season (mid May to Labour Day), contact St. Lawrence Park at 613-345-1341 .
Book a campsite at St. Lawrence Park
St. Lawrence Park Camping Rates
Daily Camping Rates (2026 Season):
Powered: $53.50
Non-powered: $46.00
Powered (Senior 55+): $48.15 (10% discount)
Non-powered (Senior 55+): $41.40 (10% discount)
Self-supported cyclist: $17.25
Weekly Camping Rates (2026 Season):
Powered: $332.00
Non-powered: $258.25
Powered (Senior 55+): $298.80 (10% discount)
Non-powered (Senior 55+): $232.43 (10% discount)
Rules and Regulations
Campfires in fire pits and fire rings only. Campfires not permitted if a fire ban is in effect.
Quiet hours are 11:00 pm to 7:00 am.
All payments for campsites must be made in full at the time of registration. Please do not set up your campsite until you have registered.
All sites will be allocated by the Park Attendant on duty. Site set up (trailer location, etc.) as directed by Park Attendant on duty.
No more than one camping unit and one dining unit may be installed per campsite without the permission of the park attendant. Maximum 6 people or one family unit comprised of parents and their minor children.
Minors (under 18 years old) are not permitted to rent a campsite.
Only one vehicle allowed at each campsite.
Only one picnic table per site.
Alcohol is prohibited in City of Brockville Parks and Trails. Alcohol is permitted on registered campsite.
Smoking is prohibited in City of Brockville Parks and Trails. Smoking permitted on registered campsite.
Pets are welcome but must be on a leash at all times. Owners are responsible for their pet’s conduct. Please clean up after your pet. Do not leave pets unattended.
No charge for guests. Guest vehicle parking is available in the parking lot. All guests must vacate park by 11:00 pm.
Campers are responsible for the actions of their children and visitors.
Campers are not permitted to cut down trees or damage park property.
Vehicles or camping equipment left unattended for 24 hours after the paid period will be removed at the owner’s expense.
The City of Brockville’s Operations Department will not accept any responsibility for loss or damage to personal property or persons, however caused.
Camper’s checkout time is 12:00 noon.
Speed limit in park is 8 kilometres per hour or 5 miles per hour.
St. Lawrence Park Campground is open from mid May until Labour Day.
Maximum camping stay is twenty-one (21) days per season.
Sorry, no refunds.
Management reserves the right to refuse admission to anyone at any time or terminate any occupant’s stay for violations of any of the above regulations, without a refund, and reserves the right to alter any regulation at any time and its decision in any situation not covered here will be final.
A pdf map of the park can be emailed to you by request.
For further information on St. Lawrence Park, during the camping season, please call 613-345-1341 .
Island Camping
Daily and seasonal camping is available on designated City of Brockville Islands . Campsites must be reserved in advance. Mooring on city docks cis also permitted and must be booked in advance. Certain campsites are designated as paddle in sites and have island access points suitable for kayaks and canoes.
Reserve an Island Campsite
Reserve dock space on an Island
Island Camping and Docking Rules
Noise:
Quiet time is observed between 11:00 pm and dawn
Only silent running generators (inverters) are permitted
No fireworks permitted on park islands
Environment:
Do not disturb or feed wildlife
Walk only on groomed trails and be mindful of ticks
Do not remove any natural or historic objects
Hunting is permitted by registered hunters on designated islands during duck hunting season
Do not collect downed trees or week
Fires are permitted in fire boxes and bit pits only. Do not leave fires unattended
All fires must be extinguished before leaving the site
Please used plastic or canned containers only
Pets:
Pets must be on a leash and under control at all times
Pets must not disturb other visitors or island wildlife
Owners must clean up after their pet and are responsible for any damage caused
Docking:
Day Use and Overnight Season Passes must always be visible
All transient docks must be booked in advance
Reservations can be made up to one week ahead, and bookings must be cancelled if plans change
Those with Seasonal Island Mooring Passes can only book one dock location per reservation. Failure to do so will result in cancellation of the entire reservation
Day Use Docking and Camping expires at 8:00 pm
Overnight Docking and Camping expires at 12:00 noon
Maximum Stay: 3 consecutive nights on one island, with no return for at least 3 consecutive days
Tenders may be moored on the side of your vessel, where possible, but they can’t be used to reserve dock spaces
Beaching or docking fees are applicable to tenders if beached or using dock space
Boats may not be left unattended overnight (from dusk to dawn)
Camping fee includes docking for the registered camper’s boat (one boat only)
Camping:
All transient campsites must be booked in advance
Camping is only available in designated areas and is not permitted on picnic islands
Each camp site is allowed a maximum of two tents (including dining tents)
A campsite accommodated a maximum of six people or single family unit (parents and their children)
Maximum stay: 7 nights and overnight camping expires at 12:00 noon on the date of departure
For paddle in sites, all canoes, kayaks, or paddleboards must be beached or placed at the campsite
The Islands are regularly patrolled by City of Brockville Bylaw Officers and failure to abide by the above rules may result in a minimum 7 day suspension.
Island Camping Regulations
The Islands are especially sensitive to damage because they are rocky, small in area and have a more severe climate than the mainland. You can contribute to the protection of the islands by complying with the following regulations:
Your Island campsite accommodates up to six people or a single family unit consisting of parents and their children.
A maximum of two tents is permitted (i.e. sleeping and dining).
Children are each camper’s responsibility.
Mooring for one boat is included in the campsite fee. Your boat must be approved and registered with the City as some docks may be inappropriate for larger boats.
Island mooring fees are applicable for all other vessels.
Visitors are welcome, subject to payment in full of mooring fees, which can be booked and paid online
Visitors must vacate the campsite by 10:00 pm. Quiet time is from 11:00 pm to 7:00 am.
Registered campers are responsible for the actions of their guests.
Visitors are required to remove all their possessions from the islands upon their departure.
Campfires are permitted in designated areas only. However, should a fire ban occur, no campfires are permitted.
Bring your own firewood.
Do not collect downed trees, limbs, brush, etc.
Do not burn downed material. This decaying matter plays an important role in the healthy development of the island forest, providing cover and food for insects, small animals and birds. Please leave them where they fall.
Campers are not permitted to damage park property.
Pets are welcome but must be on a leash at all times. Owners are completely responsible for their pet’s conduct. Please clean up after your pet.
Alcohol is only permitted on each campsite. For the safety of your family and others, please use only plastic or metal containers as broken glass is a problem due to the rockiness of the islands.
If a seasonal camper is unhappy with their site during the course of the season and no longer wishes to use it, the campsite must be returned to the City. A prorated refund of 50% will be remitted to the camper for any cancellation received prior to July 1.
The City of Brockville Islands are classified as public lands and, as such, individuals utilizing these lands are subject to all applicable municipal, provincial and federal legislation. In addition, all City of Brockville bylaws are enforced under the Provincial Offences Act and any violations will result in the immediate issuance of fines and, in some cases, the termination of campsite privileges without refund.
Please ensure your campsite is vacated and left clean by ensuring that all waste is removed. Do not leave any unwanted items such as barbecues, garbage, etc. for the City to dispose of: this is your responsibility.
Please follow “Leave no trace” principles and pack it in, pack it out processes.
Seasonal Island Camping Lottery
A limited number of seasonal campsites are available each year and are awarded through a lottery system. By the directive of City Council, first preference is given to City of Brockville residents and second preference to residents of our three surrounding townships (Augusta, Elizabethtown-Kitley, and Front of Yonge). Documentation may be required to confirm residency. Applications from other areas can also be submitted, however those names will only be drawn if there are any campsites remaining after the first and second groups.
The 2026 application deadline is Friday, May 1 st at 4:00 pm, and the 2026 draw will take place on Tuesday, May 5 th at 5:00 pm. Eligible applicants will receive a virtual meeting link by email.
Click here to apply to enter the Seasonal Island Camping Lottery .
2026 Seasonal Island Campsites
The following campsites are available for the 2026 Season:
McCoy no. 2: Assigned dock 5B; dock dimensions 20 feet by 6 feet
Cockburn no. 5: Assigned dock 9A; dock dimensions 16 feet by 5 feet
Cockburn no. 7: Assigned dock 11A, 11B; dock dimensions 20 feet by 6 feet
Cockburn no. 8: Assigned dock 12A, 12B; dock dimensions 16 feet by 5 feet
Cockburn no. 11: Assigned dock 12C, 12D; dock dimensions 16 feet by 5 feet
Cockburn no. 12: Assigned dock 13A, 13B; dock dimensions 16 feet by 5 feet
Sparrow no.13: Assigned dock 19A; dock dimensions 20 feet by 6 feet
Sparrow no. 14: Assigned dock 19B; dock dimensions 20 feet by 6 feet
Sheaffe no. 15: Assigned dock 32A, 32B; dock dimensions 20 feet by 6 feet
Sheaffe no. 16: Assigned dock 33A, 33B; dock dimensions 20 feet by 6 feet
Sheaffe no. 17: Assigned dock 34A, 34B; dock dimensions 20 feet by 6 feet
Sheaffe no. 18: Assigned dock 31A, 31B; dock dimensions 20 feet by 6 feet
De Rottenburgh no. 19: Assigned dock 22A, 22B; dock dimensions 16 feet by 5 feet
De Rottenburgh no. 20: Assigned dock 24A; dock dimensions 16 feet by 5 feet
De Rottenburgh no. 21: Assigned dock 24B; dock dimensions 16 feet by 6 feet
De Rottenburgh no. 22: Assigned dock 25B; dock dimensions 16 feet by 6 feet
De Rottenburgh no. 23: Assigned dock 23A; dock dimensions 16 feet by 5 feet
De Rottenburgh no. 25: Assigned dock 26A, 26B; dock dimensions 20 feet by 6 feet
2026 Seasonal Island Camping Lottery Overview
Residents of Brockville, as well as Augusta, Elizabethtown-Kitley, and Front of Young Townships are eligible to apply. Preference is given to City of Brockville residents and second preference is to residents of surrounding municipalities. Documentation may be required to confirm residency.
It is the City’s intention to allocate the Seasonal Campsites in a fair and equitable manner.
One application per household and per address (a household address and an individual or family member from that address cannot be on more than one Seasonal Island Camping Application).
The name drawn is the Primary Camper and, if they own a boat, it is also registered to their selected campsite. The Primary Camper must be the owner of the listed boat and their original boat registration must be provided when they complete and submit their Seasonal Island Camping Agreement (City staff will make and retain a copy of the boat registration).
Should the Primary Camper wish to share the campsite with another person or household, they are considered a Secondary Camper.
The Secondary Camper must complete and submit a Seasonal Island Camping Agreement.
A Secondary Camper can be added at any point in the season by contacting the Parks and Events Coordinator for a Seasonal Island Camping Agreement.
If the Secondary Camper owns a boat, their original boat registration must be provided when they complete and submit their Seasonal Island Camping Agreement.
The Secondary Camper is required to purchase a Seasonal Island Mooring pass from the Parks and Events Coordinator prior to the start of the season, even if the Primary Camper does not have a boat or if the Secondary Camper’s vessel is a canoe or kayak (please note that canoes, kayaks, and paddleboards are to be beached).
Each campsite has an assigned dock.
Each Primary and Secondary Camper’s boat can only be registered to one campsite.
Visitors are welcome at the campsite only if the Primary or Secondary Camper will be present for the duration of the visit.
Visitors may moor at the designated campsite dock but all visiting boats must reserve and pay for day and/or overnight mooring (by purchasing a day mooring fee, overnight mooring fee, or purchase a Seasonal Island Mooring Pass).
Visitors can moor at the designated campsite’s dock for a maximum of 7 nights but can’t return to the same Island for a minimum of 3 days after they depart (7 days on, 3 days off).
An Applicant is not allowed to be a Proxy for another Applicant. Additionally, a Proxy may only represent an Applicant at the Lottery Draw if the Applicant is unable to be present and each Proxy can only represent 1 Applicant
The City of Brockville will not be held liable for the loss or theft of any belongings from any seasonal campsite. Take note that no security or grounds patrol is provided by the City.
Click here to apply to enter the Seasonal Island Camping Lottery.

Multi-Use Recreation Facility (MURF) – Outdoor Field Components
Learn about the Outdoor Fields Component of the MURF project, including two new ball diamonds, eight pickleball courts, construction timelines, and future recreation layouts at Memorial Park. Learn more
→
Learn more
→
Dana St. Property Acquisition
The City of Brockville acquired a five-acre property on Dana Street to protect municipal infrastructure, improve public safety, and create future green space opportunities. This page provides information on the property acquisition, site improvements, and ongoing work to enhance the area for community use. Learn more
→
Learn more
→
Downtown Beautification Project
The City of Brockville is working with a consultant to develop a Downtown Beautification Plan that will guide future improvements to the downtown core. This page provides information on the project, its objectives, key milestones, and updates as the plan is developed to help create a safer, more accessible, and more welcoming downtown. Learn more
→
Learn more
→
Downtown Parking Study
The City of Brockville is undertaking a Downtown Parking Study to assess current parking conditions and plan for future needs. Funded through the 2026 Capital Budget with an allocation of $100,000, the study will evaluate parking supply, demand, and accessibility, and develop recommendations to support residents, businesses, visitors, and downtown growth. Learn more
→
Learn more
→
Specialized (Para) Transit Booking System
Brockville Transit's new Para Transit Booking System makes it easier than ever for eligible riders to book trips, track vehicles in real time, and manage their transportation through the BEST - Brockville Transit app, online portal, or by phone. Learn more
→
Learn more
→
Brockville’s “I Voted” Sticker Contest
Brockville residents are invited to submit an original design for the City's official "I Voted" sticker. The winning design will be distributed to voters during the 2026 Municipal and School Board Election and the artist will receive a $150 Visa gift card. Learn more here. Learn more
→
Learn more
→
John Taylor Park Development Project
The City of Brockville is developing John Taylor Park to honour the legacy of former Brock Trail Committee Chair John Taylor. Located adjacent to St. Paul Street and the historic Buell's Creek sluiceway. Learn more about the project details and improvements included. Learn more
→
Learn more
→
Public Citywide Portal for Service Requests and Asset Management
The City of Brockville is implementing a new Asset and Work Management System to improve how municipal assets are managed and maintained. The project includes the Citywide Portal, which allows residents to report issues related to City-owned infrastructure and assets online, while helping staff track maintenance activities, manage work orders, and support long-term planning and budgeting. Learn more
→
Learn more
→
Reynolds Park Boardwalk and Pavilion
Reynolds Park is a waterfront park in Brockville along the St. Lawrence River. The City is continuing improvements to the park, including a new pavilion and boardwalk, to create a welcoming space for residents and visitors. Learn more
→
Learn more
→
Memorial Centre Roof Renovation
Project Overview The City of Brockville is moving forward with a major rehabilitation of the Memorial Centre, beginning with the full replacement of the facility’s roof. This work is a critical first step in the long-term vision for the site as part of the City’s future Multi-Use Recreation Facility (MURF). The existing roof has reached […] Learn more
→
Learn more
→
Flag Policy Review
The public engagement period has now concluded. Public feedback informed a report to Council, which approved a new Civic Recognition and Flag Protocol Policy establishing a consistent process for community flag raisings, flag ceremonies, and proclamations. Learn more
→
Learn more
→
Bartholomew Street Reconstruction
Bartholomew Street reconstruction is underway as part of the City's 2026 Capital Budget. Learn more about the infrastructure upgrades, construction impacts, and future traffic configuration approved for the corridor. Learn more
→

Campground
The Breakwater Park Campground is located on a natural point of land, right on the waters of the Bay. Adjacent to the breakwall, seventeen sites are available, fourteen with hydro and twelve of those with water as well, and all with beautiful views of the water. A boat launch, beach, and kayak launch area are on site, and visitor parking and boat slip rentals are readily available. Our campground rates are on a daily, weekly or seasonal basis.
The Meldrum Bay Marina and Campground is owned and operated by the Dawson Citizen’s Improvement Association, a non-profit organization governed by a Board of Directors.
Campground Map
Here’s a simple map showing the general layout of the campground. Like all images on this site, click it for an enlargement.
Breakwater Park Campground Map Download

Marina
Safety
Our mandate includes the safety of our customers and employees, and signage is posted throughout the property. Please take care to leash pets and scoop any droppings. Our beach is unsupervised, so make sure your children are attended at all times. Due to our ongoing site improvements, some areas may be cordoned off to prevent mishaps. Parking and loading zones are clearly marked. Extra care should be taken when driving in the park areas, as children may be at play. Thank you for coming, and we hope you enjoy your stay!

Marina Services
The Meldrum Bay Marina is well equipped to service seasonal as well as transient boaters. Our deep water access permits the full use of our modern docks, most of which provide electricity. Gas and diesel are also conveniently available.
Our Marina Centre includes public-use showers, washrooms, laundromat, a conference room and visitors lounge, and also includes the Custom’s Office.
We are a Telephone Reporting Site / Marine, Nexus / Marine, and Canpass / Private Boat location for Canadian Border Services Agency, for international travel. As the first point of entry from the United States, the Canada Customs office is available on a 24 hour basis. Restricted hours may apply in our low season.
Seasonal dockage is based on the owner and boat as registered. Sub-letting of slips is not permitted. An extended season is available for a fee, but please note that reduced facilities are available outside of our peak season. Note that all boat trailers must be parked at the nearby Community Hall.
Marina and Campground Safety
Our mandate includes the safety of our customers and employees, and signage is posted throughout the property. Please take care to leash pets and scoop any droppings. Our beach is unsupervised, so make sure your children are attended at all times. Due to our ongoing site improvements, some areas may be cordoned off to prevent mishaps. Parking and loading zones are clearly marked. Extra care should be taken when driving in the park areas, as children may be at play. Thank you for coming, and we hope you enjoy your stay!

City Services
City Campground
Nelson City Campground
The City of Nelson Campground is scheduled to close on October 16th. The last night of camping will be the night of October 15th!
Nelson City Campground office hours Are 8:00 AM – 8:00 PM. Friday October 16th hours will be 8:00am-4:00pm
The City of Nelson Campground operates within the City of Nelson boundary as per Bylaw No. 3268 Section 5.6 No natural fires are permitted on our property.
If you have questions please give us a call and we will be able to assist you.
Reservations
In order to finalize a reservation booking at the City of Nelson Campground, staff require the following personal information.
The number of people in your party
The names of all your party members, particularly if you are arriving separately
A phone number by which we can reach the party lead
The date of arrival and departure
License plate number for all vehicles parked on our premises
A description of your tent, trailer, motor home, or van (so we can select an appropriate site)
Full payment is required at the time of booking
Reserve by emailing campground@nelson.ca or calling 250-352-7618 or by visiting https://letscamp.ca/camps/nelson-city-campground .
Privacy Policy
The City of Nelson collects your information in accordance with Section 26 of the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act. The City of Nelson collects your information for the purposes of administering City of Nelson programs and services, including permits and licensing services. By providing your personal information over the phone, by email or through the online booking system you are agreeing with this privacy statement.
Max Stay Policy
To ensure as many guests as possible have the opportunity to enjoy the Nelson City Campground, the maximum stay is 14 consecutive nights .
Features
The Nelson City Campground offers visitors access to a forested, natural environment in an urban setting. Located on High Street, just east of downtown Nelson, the campground is centrally located and within walking distance to shopping, parks, and the beach.
The campground now offers bags of cubed ice for sale. Anyone can purchase ice; you do not need to be a guest in the campground.
The campground operates from May 1st - to October 16th. Shared laundry, cooking facilities, bathrooms and showers, and tourist information are available on-site. The campground offers 5 full-service sites; 9 sites with electrical only hookup; 5 sites with electrical and water hookup; 20 tent sites.
We offer a convenient on-site sani dump station—locals and guests are welcome to use it during office hours.
Note: Shaw Go Wi-Fi is available in the campground and other public areas around Nelson. Find more information on Shaw Go Wi-Fi Guest Access .
Wildlife Policy
All camp guests visiting our campground MUST have a secure storage system for food items throughout the duration of their stay. Examples of secure storage can be but not limited to your RV or vehicle.
Camp guests without proper food storage systems will be offered a full refund upon check-in.
Campground staff are committed to the safety and well-being of all camp guests, staff, community members, and visitors to our region.
All food attractants must be eliminated to reduce human-wildlife interactions. Thank you!
Extreme Weather - Wildfire and Smoke policy
Extreme Weather, Wildfire & Smoke Policy: The City of Nelson Campground's standard 7-day cancellation and refund policy remains in effect during periods of wildfire activity, smoke, or other extreme weather conditions. Refunds will not be provided for cancellations made within 7 days of arrival due to smoke, poor air quality, or personal travel decisions. Exceptions may be considered only if a major road closure prevents reasonable access to the campground, an evacuation order affects the campground or travel route, or the local air quality reaches an Extreme Risk level as determined by Environment and Climate Change Canada or other applicable authorities. The campground will remain open unless directed to close by emergency officials, and guests are encouraged to monitor current wildfire conditions and air quality before travelling.
Refund Policy
7 days before Check-in: Notice of cancellation is required; full refund. If no notice of cancellation is received at least 7days in advance, there is no refund given.
Personal Item Storage Policy
All personal items left behind at the City of Nelson Campground will be stored onsite for 30 days. After this period, any unclaimed items will be discarded.
Thank you for your cooperation.
Electric Vehicle (EV) Charging Information
Please note that the Nelson City Campground electrical sites can not support EV charging. However, there are several convenient charging stations located nearby:
• Nelson & District Community Complex – 305 Hall Street (closest option)
• Prestige Lakeside Resort – 701 Lakeside Drive (along the waterfront)
• Nelson & District Chamber of Commerce – 91 Baker Street
We recommend planning your charging needs in advance to ensure a smooth and enjoyable stay.
Campground Fees
The Corporation of the City of Nelson Fees and Charges Amendment (Tourist Park) Bylaw No. 3605, 2024 was passed and adopted on July 2, 2024 and outlines the following updated fees:
Tent Platform - 10ft x 10ft (forest area) $26.00/night
Unserviced Site (tent with no hook-ups) $30.00/night
Partial Serviced Site (electricity Site (electricity only) $40.00/night
Services Site (electricity and water) $45.00/night
Full Service Site (electricity, water, sewer) $50.00/night
Sani-dump - Campers $10.00/use
Sani-dump - Non-campers $15.00/use

Downtown Parking Strategy
Council formally approved the 2021 Downtown Parking Strategy on March 9, 2021.
Click here to read the 2021 Downtown Parking Strategy
The major features of the attached strategy include:
The “Context” chapter provides background information on parking in Nelson and the theory of parking policy approaches.
A summary of all consultation undertaken and a summary of the survey results. More detailed information from the survey is included in Appendix B and C.
Eleven “Guiding Principles for Decisions on Parking” (pages 15-17). These principles seek to balance all residents’ needs, define the City’s role in parking management, underscore the City’s commitment to financial sustainability, and provide support for active transportation, and the transition to electric vehicles
Sixty-one “Recommended Actions” (beginning on page 19) under thirteen headers:
Maximize Current Parking Assets
Financial Sustainability
Park-and-Ride
City Parkade
Downtown Residential Streets
Residential Guest Permits
Making Parking Easier through Customer Service
Parking Requirements
Veterans and Seniors Parking (no actions proposed)
Carsharing
Tradesperson and Commercial Delivery
Effective Enforcement and Increased Compliance
Electric Vehicles
An implementation table recommending which actions should be pursued in the short, medium, and long term (Appendix A; page 35).
A downtown parking strategy establishes a clear, goal-driven framework for the community that will assist staff in decisions and policy projects related to parking. The strategy is designed to help the City to achieve its sustainability goals, including economic, social, and environment goals. It continues to recognize that convenient and accessible parking in the downtown that has regular turnover is critical to downtown businesses. It is complementary to the Nelson Next climate plan, the Active Transportation Plan, the Downtown Urban Design Strategy, transit planning, and the West Kootenay 100% Renewable Energy Plan.

Lakeside Camping
Burton Historical Park / 2014/03/05
The campground will open on May 1 – October 15th, 2026.
Welcome to Burton’s family-oriented campground situated on the shores of the Arrow Lakes. We are 22 km north of the Needles Ferry and 36 km west of Nakusp on Highway 6 towards Fauquier.
We have 37 sites which are mostly treed; some sites are pull through.
There are large open areas for recreation; a volleyball net, horseshoe pit, and space for bocce is available for use.
Sites A, B, 1 to 8 and 25 to 35 are serviced sites (power/water) that are reserved on a single sleeping unit basis. Please review our campground policy on adding additional sleeping units to your reservation.
Sites 9 to 17 – Non-Serviced -Small Sleeping Unit/Tenting area , are 1 unit only sites and camping unit must be 19 ft or less. If you book a longer unit into these sites, you will find that you don’t have a site when you arrive.
Waterfront sites 18 to 24 are non-serviced sites that are reserved on a single sleeping unit basis. Please review our campground policy on adding additional sleeping units to your reservation.
Additional Sleeping Units – Our site reservation fee covers 1 sleep unit and car/truck only. You must call in advance for approval if you would like to add an extra unit to your site reservation. All requests for including an additional sleeping unit to your reservation must be approved to ensure everyone will safely fit, to have their reservation details include your guest’s name for checking in and ensure everyone is aware of the additional fees that will be charged for each sleeping unit added –
**There is no extra fee for a child’s tent (17 years old and younger) if in a reserved site and no additional vehicles have joined site.
Enter SR2026 in the Promo Code to receive the Senior discount (65+)
All registered guests are welcome to use our hot shower facilities free of charge. If you are a non-guest to the campground, there is a $4.00 charge to use this campground amenity.
Sani Dump available on site. There is an $10.00 charge per dump, if you wish to use this campground extra. The use of the sani-dump is not included in your reservation fee, and can be paid by cash, debit or credit card at the time of use.
**If you are looking for a site less then 24 hours before check in – please call for availability, or email reservation@burtonhistoricalpark.com with Name, Phone Number, Check In/Out date request, how long your sleeping unit (tent, trailer, rv) is, and if you require a serviced site.**
***REFUNDS WILL NOT BE PROVIDED OUTSIDE OF REFUND POLICY (no less then 7 nights prior to check in) FOR WEATHER, SMOKE, OR WATER LEVELS***
To book a site please visit our reservations page .
2014/03/05 in Lakeside Camping , Main .

Pricing
Nightly rates:
Serviced $40, Seniors (65+) $38
Unserviced $33, Seniors (65+) $31
All sites are reserved on a single sleeping unit basis and covers the cost of one sleeping unit, and one vehicle.
Additional sleeping units can be added to your site upon approval and additional sleeping unit rates applied. Please call in to discuss this option, as we confirm everyone will safely fit and names are added to reservations. We can not add any additional people/sleeping units to a reservation without the approval of the person who reserved the site.
All full rate reservations are permitted 1 kids tent within their site with no additional charge. A kids tent is for kids 17 and younger who are staying within a reserved site – this free tent is only available to those who do not have any additional vehicles joining their site.
Additional vehicles added to reserved sites without an additional sleeping unit will be charged $15.00/night – unless the additional vehicle is being slept in. Any sleeping unit with a vehicle will be charged the nightly rate. This includes sleeping in the vehicle, a hammock or anywhere other then the sleeping unit attached to the reservation.
5% GST included
Check-in 1:00 pm
Check-out 11:00 am
Firewood: $10/Bundle and includes kindling.
Sani-dump: $10.00 for registered guests
Bookings open up at 12.01am on Jan 1st, 2026. Phones will only be answered on Fridays, and messages and emails will be answered daily until season opens on May 1st.
There is a maximum stay of 14 days during high season (July 1 – August 31).
Stays during the shoulder seasons are unlimited (May 15- Jun 30, Sep 1 – Oct 14).
2 Group Sites are available for 10 or more sleeping units during high season and long weekends, and will accommodate smaller groups during should season – These sites are non-serviced and can be reserved a year in advance. Please make prior arrangements by phone or email.
When you reserve your site(s), we ask for payment in full for each site. Visa and MasterCard are accepted.
Only the person whose name is on the reservation has access to change or cancel a reservation.
If a cancellation is made 7 or more nights before your scheduled arrival date, the camping fees will be fully refunded (excluding the booking fee). If a cancellation is made less than 7 nights before your scheduled arrival date, all fees are forfeited. Refunds are not given for an eviction, vacating your site early or inclement weather.

Quatse Regional Campground
Book your stay today and be part of a place where comfort meets the wild: Book Online Here
Come for the nature, stay for the experience! Nestled in the heart of the forest and set along the peaceful banks of the Quatse River, the Quatse campground offers the perfect balance of wilderness escape and travel comfort. Whether you’re pitching a tent beneath the pines or settling in with your RV, you’ll find yourself surrounded by towering trees, met by bird songs and the calm that only nature can offer.
We’re pleased to share that all campground facilities are now open, including:
Coin-operated, pay-per-use laundry services
Flush washrooms
Hot showers
Potable water
Sani-dump
Known for our clean, well-kept amenities and the welcoming experience that brings visitors back year after year, the Quatse campground is proud to offer both rustic beauty and thoughtful service.
Rates and Reservations
To book, please visit: https://letscamp.ca/camps/quatse-regional-campground
Seasonal Dates
Reservations open the first Monday of February each year. The campsite opens for guests on the May long weekend and is open until September 30. You are welcome to stay a maximum of 14 days per reservation.

Unincorporated Communities Bylaws
Unincorporated Communities Bylaws
There are a number of areas and unincorporated communities within the RDMW that are subject to their own Official Community Plan Bylaws and/or Zoning Bylaws. These locations may also be subject to the requirement to obtain a Building Permit or Site Permit as a prelude to undertaking the construction of buildings and structures.
Alder Bay
Alder Bay is comprised of one property totalling 11.88 hectares (29.4 acres) which is operated as a campground, marina and boat launch (Alder Bay Resort). Alder Bay is subject to Regional District of Mount Waddington Alder Bay Resort Land Use Bylaw No. 491. The Land Use Bylaw prescribes detailed regulations related to land use, the siting, size and dimensions of buildings, minimum lot size for the purposes of subdivision, etc. Please refer to the following link for more information:
Regional District of Mount Waddington Alder Bay Resort Land Use Bylaw No. 491
While approval of a Building Permit is not required, the siting of buildings and structures must be undertaken in accordance with the BC Building Code and a Building Bylaw is in effect that requires a Site Permit be applied for and issued by the Regional District. The Site Permit process is designed to ensure that the siting of buildings and structures conforms to the requirements of the applicable zoning bylaw. Please refer to the following links for more information:
Building Bylaw No. 682, 2003 (Consolidated)
Application for Site Permit
Example Site Plan to Accompany Application for Building or Site Permit
Owners Acknowledgment of Responsibility – Site Permit
Coal Harbour
The community of Coal Harbour is subject to an Official Community Plan Bylaw (Bylaw No. 657, 2002) and a Zoning Bylaw (Bylaw No. 669, 2002). The Official Community Plan includes objectives and policies to guide decisions related to planning and land use management for the community into the future. The Zoning Bylaw is intended to implement the objectives and policies of the Official Community Plan and prescribes detailed regulations related to land use, the siting, size and dimensions of buildings, minimum lot size for the purposes of subdivision, etc. Please refer to the following links for more information:
Official Community Plan:

Building Bylaw:
The siting of buildings and structures in Coal Harbour must be undertaken in accordance with the BC Building Code, and a Building Bylaw is in effect that requires a Building Permit be applied for and issued by the Regional District. The Building Permit process is designed to ensure that the siting of buildings and structures conforms to the requirements of the BC Building Code and the applicable zoning bylaw. Welcome to the
Beautiful North Island
Your resource for living & working in the Regional District of Mount Waddington.
Established in June 1966, the Regional District of Mount Waddington (RDMW) serves the various communities & municipalities within the Mount Waddington regional district. The RDMW provides local services, planning, solid waste, parks, economic and tourism development services for the residents & businesses on the traditional territories of the Kwakwa̱ka̱ʼwakw First Nations.

We’re Hiring! Join Our Team
The Regional District of Mount Waddington is currently recruiting for multiple exciting positions across our organization.
If you’re looking for a new opportunity, want to build your career on the North Island, or know someone who would be a great fit, we’d love to hear from you.
Explore our current opportunities and find your next role with the RDMW.

The RDMW provides local services, planning, solid waste, parks, economic and tourism development services for the residents & businesses on the traditional territories of the Kwakwa̱ka̱ʼwakw First Nations.

BRAUN'S ISLAND RV PARK
ABOUT
ABOUT
Inspired by the surrounding landscape, Braun's Island RV Park was designed to make your visit a unique, comfortable and fun experience. Our sites are spacious and our rates are competitive.
Call or email islandrv@citywest.ca to inquire about monthly rates.
Our team knows that travelling can be exhausting, and will do their best to make your stay easy and satisfying. Take a look at our site to find out more about our sites and amenities, and get in touch if there’s anything else we can help you with. We look forward to welcoming you soon!
ROOMS
OUR SITES
Our sites are nestled in a private area with nature at your doorstep. Large treed sites or wide open sites for family game nights or group get togethers can be found at Braun's Island RV Park. We welcome fully self contained RV's ,
*Air tight 4" threaded sewer connection is MANDATORY at our park.
*All RV's must be 20 yrs old or less and in good condition.
*No stand alone tents allowed.
*Monthly stays available at $ 800.00 per month for each site (April - September only)
Book a Site
OUR SERVICES
OUR SERVICES
Shower & Laundry
With our Shower Facilities, guests enjoy the highest level of comfort at no costs. For your convenience we offer plenty of coin operated washers and dryers within a spacious newly renovated laundry room.
Free Wifi
​
We’re happy to provide our guests with a range of amenities to meet their specific needs. Wifi is available to most sites.
Vehicle Access/Pull Thru Sites
Braun's Island RV Park provides you with the amenities you need for an enjoyable outdoor experience. Take advantage of our Vehicle Access and other benefits when you decide to stay with us.

THINGS TO DO
Hiking & Biking Trails
The area is rich with hiking and biking trails for everyone, from beginner to advanced.
Skeena Valley Farmers Market
Terrace is known for its very large and diverse group of artisan vendors. Check them out from May through October in George Little Park.
River Tours
Terrace and Kitimat boast lush rivers and their many tributaries making this a one of a kind scenic adventure.
Skeena Valley Golf & Country Club
Skeena Valley Golf & Country Club is an 18 hole course which lies at the foot of majestic Thornhill Mountain just 10 minutes from your RV site.
Arts & Culture
Terrace is home to a vibrant art and music community. Regular exhibitions by talented local artists can be viewed at the Terrace Art Gallery, Red Raven and local coffee shops .
Ocean Fishing
Go for a guided fishing charter on Kitimat or Prince Rupert with one of the areas many fine fishing guide companies.

Peace Island Park
250.789.9295
The Peace Island Park RV and tenting campground opens in May with end-of-season closure weather-dependent. This is a scenic island getaway on the shores of the Peace River, and features many amenities for the whole family with serviced, non-serviced and group sites available.
About the Campground
There are 40 non-powered sites on the island, with 57 serviced sites in the new expansion area, and 24 full serviced sites new to the park.
This campground is one of the most affordable campgrounds in BC, with fees ranging from $22 to $88.
Park features include:
Picnic / Day Use Area
Walking Trails
Horseshoe Pits
Historic Rocky Mountain Forts
Playgrounds
Shelter with Cookhouse
Firewood
Boat Launch
Beautiful Outdoor Pavilion (reservation required)
Book With Us!
Already booked?
Check out our printable camping guide for more information on park rules, rates and more.
Printable Camping Guide
We want to hear from you!
For feedback, complaints, noise disturbances, wildlife reporting, and more, please fill out our online feedback form.
Provide Feedback
Park Rules
All campers must check in at our office, this includes group site users.
Trailers must be parked no less than 15 feet (4.5 meters) apart.
Campers and vehicles must fit entirely within the confines of your campsite. Please do not block or park on roadways.
Quiet time begins at 11pm.
All dogs must be on a leash. Owners are responsible for cleaning up after their pets.
ATVs are permitted only in designated areas, and must be trailered in and out of the park.
Fireworks are not permitted in the park.
Discharge of firearms is not permitted in the park.
Please report all bear sightings to the Conservation Officer at 1-877-952-7277.
Adherence to current provincial fire restrictions is required. Check with our office or the Province of BC website.
Check in and check out
Check in times begin at 12pm
Check out is 11am
Quad site check in is 2pm
Quad site check out is 1pm
Quiet time begins at 11pm
Park Rates
Non-power sites $22/unit/night
Power sites $27/unit/night
Full Service sites $42/unit/night
Quad Sites $88/night up to 4 units, extra units are $22/unit/night

Taber Municipal Park
i
A Fire Advisory is in Effect.
Due to current hot, dry conditions and continued dry weather in the forecast, the Municipal District of Taber has issued a Fire Advisory for all municipal boundaries, effective immediately and until further notice. Learn more.
Nestled along the serene banks of the Oldman River, Taber Municipal Park and Campground offers an unparalleled escape into nature. Here, you'll discover a diverse range of recreational activities and pristine facilities spread across our expansive 60-acre property. Choose from spacious, shaded pull-through or back-in sites, lush grassy tent areas, and pristine bathrooms, ensuring your camping experience is comfortable and enjoyable. As a bonus, we provide complimentary firewood, so you can gather around the campfire and create unforgettable memories.
Beyond the campsite, our park boasts a wide array of amenities, including sand volleyball, horseshoe pits, a playground, and a baseball diamond for endless family fun. Adventurers will be delighted by the proximity to the
MD of Taber Coulee Trail System
, perfect for hiking and mountain biking, while water enthusiasts can paddle, fish, or swim along the river's tranquil shores. Whether you're planning an intimate family outing, a group adventure, a memorable wedding, or simply seeking a solo escape to reconnect with nature, Taber Municipal Park and Campground is the ideal destination to bask in the great outdoors. Come and make cherished memories with loved ones in this breathtaking natural haven.
We've Switched!
New Online Booking & Payment System Now Live
We’ve recently switched to Let’s Camp Reservation Software to make booking your stay at Taber Municipal Park easier than ever!
✅ To book your site, you must first create a Let’s Camp account.
✅ Once you’ve selected your site, don’t forget to go to your shopping cart to complete your reservation and payment. This final step confirms your booking.
With limited spaces available, we recommend booking early to avoid disappointment.
Plan your visit with ease—just a few clicks and you’re set!

CONTACT INFORMATION & RATES
Contact
For ALL cancellations and site changes, please email the Park office: mdpark@mdtaber.ab.ca
Park office (May to October): 1-403-223-0091
Administration office (November to April): 1-403-223-3541
Hours of operation
Park office open from 11:00 am to 8:00 pm – 7 days a week
Campground gates open from 7:00 am to 9:00 pm
The top gate of the park is open 24-7
Camping rates
Individual Sites:
$40 per night
All sites have been upgraded to 30-amp power.
Group Use rates
All Group-Use area rentals include a camp kitchen, firewood, and plugins. Group-Use "A" and "B" rentals include pit toilets and potable water.
Group-Use Areas “A” and “B”:
$160 per night
Check-in time 2:00 pm
Check-out time is 11:00 am the following day
Group Use "C" (daytime rental only):
$40 per day
Available from 2:00 pm to 10:00 pm the same day
To book a Group Use area, please refer to the ‘Terms of Service’ blue (+) tab below.
Address

Expand the blue (+) tabs below to learn more.
Map of Campsites
Download the PDF version here.
Amphitheatre Booking Guidelines
Please note
The Taber Municipal Park Amphitheatre is part of Group-Use Area C.
Groups less than 25 people:
Group-Use Area "C" is used for hosting smaller events with the amphitheatre. Booking includes a small camp kitchen, picnic tables and several electrical plugs around the amphitheatre.
Parking is limited, so visitors must park in the Day-Use parking lot and walk to the event. The nearest washroom facilities are located east in the Day-Use Area. (No lighting or sound equipment is provided with the rental.)
Community groups hosting events are responsible for their own security (1 security person per 25 participants) and clean up after the event. Failure to do so will result in extra charges billed at $100.00/hour for park contractors to clean the area.
The MD will provide safety vests to event volunteers, and barricades if asked for in advance. Extra garbage receptacles are also available if needed.
All park bylaws remain in effect.
Groups more than 25 people:
To accommodate an event larger than 25 people, both Group-Use "C" (theater) and Group-Use "B" must be booked together.
Reserving Group-Use "C" includes the amphitheatre area as described above. (No lighting or sound equipment is provided with the rental.)
Reserving Group-Use "B" includes the grassed area, a larger parking lot closer to the amphitheatre, closer washroom facilities, and a larger camp kitchen with extra electrical plugs.
Community groups hosting events are responsible for their own security (1 security person per 25 participants) and clean up after the event. Failure to do so will result in extra charges billed at $100.00/hour for park contractors to clean the area.
Community Groups are responsible for purchasing their own insurance coverage.
The MD will provide safety vests to event volunteers, and barricades if asked for in advance. Extra garbage receptacles are also available if needed.
All park bylaws remain in effect in Group-Use Areas.
Terms of Service
Municipal District of Taber – Parks and Recreation Areas
Municipal Parks and Recreation Areas Bylaw No. 1974 of the Municipal District of Taber applies to all Parks and Recreation areas within the MD of Taber, except where any provincial statute of Alberta or any agreement involving the MD of Taber provides otherwise.
Camping
4 Campsites are available on a first-come, first-served basis for single-night usage. The remaining campsites are by reservation only.
Approved camping accommodation units include:
Tents, trailers, tent trailers, motorhomes, fifth wheels with a truck, vans, truck campers, and registered motor vehicles including a truck or car used by a person as shelter equipment while camping.
Campground checkout time is 12:00 Noon. Check-in time is 2:00 pm.
20 km/h is the maximum speed limit within the park.
Camping is restricted to those areas designated for overnight camping and the group-use areas and is subject to the applicable fees.
ONLY registered campers are allowed in the shower houses.
Permitted On A Campsite
Maximum eight (8) persons per individual campsite, unless they are all members of a single-family unit.
Two (2) family units of NOT MORE than eight (8) people may occupy an individual campsite.
Two (2) vehicles are allowed per site. Do not park on grass areas.
Visitors to the campsite MUST use the parking lot by the day-use area.
Alcohol is permitted in designated areas only such as designated campsites and group-use areas upon rental.
Not Permitted
Do not litter – please use the receptacles provided to dispose of any refuse.
Do not deface or destroy any property or vegetation that the MD of Taber has erected or caused to be erected.
Do not park on grass areas – please stay off grass with trailers and motor vehicles. Only tents are allowed on grass areas.
ATV use is not permitted. All motor vehicles must remain on designated roadways, except for those required by Municipal employees to carry out their duties in the Parks and Recreation Areas.
No fireworks or explosives of any type – do not discharge paintball guns except in an area designated for this purpose.
No soliciting – unless prior written approval has been obtained from the MD of Taber.
No pig roasts are allowed in the park.
Be a Good Neighbour
Quiet hours are 11:00 pm to 7:00 am.
All visitors must leave before 11:00 pm.
Avoid excessive noises that would disrupt people sleeping so that everyone can enjoy the peace and tranquillity of our park.
Parents must accompany any children away from the campsite during this time.
Generator hours are from 9:00 – 11:00 am and 6:00 – 8:00 pm.
Group-Use
We have three Group-Use Areas that are available by reservation, Group-Use "A", "B" and "C".
Group-Use Area rentals include use of camp kitchen, firewood and plugins. Group-Use "A" and "B" also include pit toilets and potable water
.
Group-Use Areas “A” and “B” – $100 daytime rental only. Available Sunday – Thursday. Use promo code “evening” when booking. Check-in time at 2:00 pm. Check-out time at 10:00 pm the same day.
How to book using promo code.
Search for the evening that you would like to book (available Sunday through Wednesday only). To process the booking, you must choose the following day as the checkout. For example, if you chose the evening of Sunday, September 12th, you must choose Monday, September 13th as the check-out date.
Choose either Group use A or B for your booking and select Add to Cart. If no Group Use sites are found in the search, this indicates that they are not available for booking that evening.
Click on the Review Cart button, followed by the Proceed to Checkout button.
Fill in all of the required Guest information. Please indicate that this booking is for a Sunday evening only in the Special Needs or Requests box. Then click Continue to Payment Amount.
Click the Enter a promo code button. In the box that opens, enter EVENING . The discount will automatically apply to the order total.
Click the Continue to Payment Method button and enter your credit card information. Click Place Order to complete the booking.
Group-Use Areas “A” and “B” – $160 for overnight rental. Check-in time at 2:00 pm. Check-out time at 11:00 am the following day.
Group-Use "C" – $40 per day from 2:00 pm to 10:00 pm.
Day-Use
Available for public use from 7:00 am until 11:00 pm only.
No alcoholic beverages are allowed in the day-use area.
Fires
Fires shall NEVER be left unattended.
Fires must be confined to fireplaces or appliances provided or in any portable appliance, and then only at designated locations.
Fires must be COMPLETELY OUT and cool when leaving, and can only be fueled with seasoned wood, charcoal, coal, natural gas or propane.
Fire ban notices may be issued due to dry weather conditions.
Pets
Dogs and cats are welcome but must be on a leash at all times.
Please pick up after your pets.
Please note
No person shall interfere with the right of others to the quiet and peaceful enjoyment of the Municipal Parks or Recreation Areas through nuisance activities as defined in the Bylaw – any individual determined a "Nuisance" through drunkenness, use of obscene, offensive or insulting language, fighting or disorderly conduct, disruptive partying, excessively loud music, voice or something or someone being disruptively noisy, may be asked to leave.
A person who enters the Municipal Parks and Recreation Areas shall comply with any lawful orders and instructions made or issued by a Police Officer, Bylaw Enforcement Officer, a Municipal District of Taber employee and Municipal Park employees.
Any person who refuses to leave the Municipal Parks and Recreation Areas after having been asked to do so by a Bylaw Enforcement Officer, an RCMP Officer, or a Municipal Park Employee or its agents, may be issued a Violation Ticket and if they remain, may be removed from the Municipal Parks and Recreation Areas.
Where a Bylaw Enforcement Officer has reasonable grounds to believe that a provision of this Bylaw has been contravened, that Bylaw Enforcement Officer is authorized and empowered to issue a Violation Ticket to any person the Bylaw Enforcement Officer has reasonable grounds to believe is responsible for the contravention.
A Violation Ticket shall be served upon any such Person personally or by leaving it with a person who has the appearance of being at least eighteen (18) years of age.
A Violation Ticket shall state the name of the person; the date of issuance; a description of the offence, the section number of the Bylaw, and the date on which the offence occurred; the appropriate penalty for the offence as specified in Schedule "A" of this Bylaw; that the penalty shall be paid within thirty (30) days of the issuance of the Violation Ticket; and any other information as may be required by the Municipal Administrator.
Please note
The employees, servants, and agents of the Municipal District of Taber, while acting in the course of their employment or duty, are exempt from the provisions of this Bylaw.
Cancellation & Refund Policy
At Taber Municipal Park & Campground, we embrace all the beauty nature has to offer, rain or shine!
Please note
We are unable to provide credits or refunds for weather-related conditions.
For cancellations made more than 24 hours before your scheduled arrival, a $20 cancellation fee will apply. The remaining balance will be refunded to the credit card on file.
For cancellations made within 24 hours of your scheduled arrival, a charge equivalent to one night's stay will apply. The remaining balance will be refunded to the credit card on file.
In the case of early departures, an additional charge equivalent to one night's stay beyond the departure date will apply. The remaining balance will be refunded to the credit card on file.
Please be aware that no-shows will be charged the full amount of their reservation.
For your convenience, all cancellations must be made over the phone.
Thank you for choosing Taber Municipal Park & Campground. We look forward to hosting you!

A Fire Advisory is in Effect.
Due to current hot, dry conditions and continued dry weather in the forecast, the Municipal District of Taber has issued a Fire Advisory for all municipal boundaries, effective immediately and until further notice.
While the Fire Advisory is in effect, residents and visitors are advised that there is an elevated risk of wildfire.
Safe campfires are allowed on public land, in campgrounds, and on private land.
A fire permit must be obtained before burning. Apply for a fire permit online here.
Fire permits may be restricted or suspended.
Anyone conducting a controlled burn is urged to exercise extreme caution and closely monitor conditions at all times.
The Municipal District of Taber will continue to monitor weather and fire risk conditions and will adjust the advisory as necessary. Corporate Services
Corporate Services (also known as the Finance and Administration Department) provides a wide and varied range of services to ratepayers, Councillors, and all internal departments within the Municipal District of Taber.
Services offered
Assessments
Access to Information and Protection of Privacy
Accounts Payable and Receivable
Community Funding (grants)
Financial Reporting
Operating and Capital Budgets
Property Taxes
Contact
For more information on the services provided by Corporate Services, contact:
Mike Passey
Director, Corporate Services
Email
Monday to Friday from 8:00 am – 4:30 pm
Expand the blue (+) tabs below to learn more.
Financial reporting and budgets
Financial reporting and budgets
In an attempt to be as transparent to the public as possible, Corporate Services provides multiple reports to keep our ratepayers informed of where their tax dollars are being spent. These include financial reports such as the MD of Taber’s annual financial statements, operating and capital budgets, and annual Financial Reports .
The approved Operating and Capital Budgets are also available to the public, as these budgets are established by Council to guide the operations of the MD of Taber.
As part of the budget process, Council reviews multiple applications for funding from organizations throughout the MD of Taber. In order to effectively review these applications, Council has established Recreation Boards for each of the districts within the MD of Taber. These Recreation Boards assist the organizations with the preparation of their applications and provide recommendations to Council for their districts' Recreation and Cultural Funding .
Property taxes and assessments
Property taxes and assessments
Municipal Taxes are generated in order to fund the operations of the Municipal District of Taber. The MD of Taber is also responsible for collecting taxes for funding Education and Seniors Housing requisitions.
The MD of Taber is responsible for ensuring that each property owner pays his or her fair share of taxes. Property Assessments are used by municipalities to distribute the tax burden among property owners in a municipality. The total assessed value of all the properties in the MD of Taber is used to determine the tax rate, which is then able to be applied equally to the ratepayers of the MD of Taber. Tax Bylaws are established each year to fund municipal operations and requisitions.
To assist our ratepayers with making payments on their property taxes, the MD of Taber offers the ability to enter into our Tax Instalment Payment Plan (TIPP) , which allows for pre-authorized monthly payments to be made on their taxes.
Tax Certificates are also available through Corporate Services and provide details on tax balances for tax roll accounts, typically used by lawyers and banking institutions as a confirmation of tax balances; however, these are also available to the landowners of the property.
Financial services
Financial services
Corporate Services provides multiple financial services for the MD of Taber, including payroll, accounts payable and receivable , utility billing, and records management. Also included within this department are administrative staff that manages public inquiries, the main phone lines, and the reception counter at the administration office.
Community funding (grants)
Community funding (grants)
The MD of Taber provides support and assistance to organisations within the MD of Taber for grants research and application . The MD of Taber will search for grants relating to a group's particular project or program. With the ever-increasing strain on municipal budgets, grants from both provincial and federal governments and the private sector are a great alternative source of funding for organisations. To discuss grant options for your organization, please contact Corporate Services at 4 03-223-3541 .

A Fire Advisory is in Effect.
Due to current hot, dry conditions and continued dry weather in the forecast, the Municipal District of Taber has issued a Fire Advisory for all municipal boundaries, effective immediately and until further notice.
While the Fire Advisory is in effect, residents and visitors are advised that there is an elevated risk of wildfire.
Safe campfires are allowed on public land, in campgrounds, and on private land.
A fire permit must be obtained before burning. Apply for a fire permit online here.
Fire permits may be restricted or suspended.
Anyone conducting a controlled burn is urged to exercise extreme caution and closely monitor conditions at all times.
The Municipal District of Taber will continue to monitor weather and fire risk conditions and will adjust the advisory as necessary. The goal of the advisory is to raise public awareness of the increased fire danger, help protect people and property, and reduce the risk of costly emergency responses.

Council Strategic Priorities Plan
The Municipal District of Taber's Strategic Priorities Plan gives Council a clear path to follow as itworks toward a strong future for residents. It reflects the direction Council wants to take and will helpguide the choices made over this term, keeping attentionon what matters most to the municipality and the peoplewho live here. Council is committed to using this plan as aguide for the decisions ahead, so the Municipal District ofTaber can keep moving forward in a way that is thoughtful,steady, and built for the future.
MD of Taber Council Strategic Priorities Plan 2026–2029
Now
•
Land Management Strategy
Project in Progress. A strategy and policy to guide the management of municipally owned lands, including leases for Cultivation (Dryland and Irrigation), Grazing, and Tax Recovery Grazing. For more information visit: mdtaber.ab.ca/p/lmp
Equitable Taxation Plan
Develop and promote a fair and equitable taxation plan that contributes to the long-term financial success of the municipality.
Community Engagement
Continue to foster and support community engagement initiatives.
Update Strategic Communications Plan
Enhance the MD of Taber's communication strategy to be more representative of our population
.
Complete Asset Management Plan
Complete the MD’s asset management strategy so that Council can make informed decisions on the long-term infrastructure needs of the Municipal District of Taber. This involves determining what assets are in place, where they are located, and assessing the condition of the assets.
Next
•
Business Attraction and Retention Plan
Finalize our Economic Development priorities and implement a business attraction and retention plan.
Industrial Park Development
Develop an Industrial Park that will attract industry to the area.
Long-term Financial Plan
Create a long-term financial strategy for the replacement of existing infrastructure and development of new infrastructure to support our growth into the future.
Later
•
Regional Recreation Facility Planning
Develop a regional plan for the administration, maintenance and funding of the recreation facilities in the municipality.
Recreation Service Delivery Review
Explore an Alternative Service Delivery model (ASD) for recreation that will reinforce existing partnerships, establish new ones, and ultimately ensure sustainable and equitable recreation opportunities for all residents in the Municipal District of Taber.
Expand the blue (+) tabs below to learn more.
A Healthy, Active,and Vibrant Community
Strategic Priorities:
Regional Recreation Facility Planning — Develop a regional plan for the administration, maintenance and funding of the recreation facilities in the municipality.
Recreation Service Delivery Review — Explore an Alternative Service Delivery model (ASD) for recreation that will reinforce existing partnerships, establish new ones, and ultimately ensure sustainable and equitable recreation opportunities for all residents in the Municipal District of Taber.
Revenue Growth Driven By Diversification
Strategic Priorities
Land Management Strategy — Finalize the Land Management Strategy.
Equitable Taxation Plan — Develop and promote a fair and equitable taxation plan that contributes to the long-term financial success of the municipality.
Business Attraction and Retention Plan — Finalize our Economic Development priorities and implement a business attraction and retention plan.
Industrial Park Development — Develop an Industrial Park that will attract industry to the area.
A Supportive, Diverse, and RespectfulCommunity
Strategic Priorities
Community Engagement — Continue to foster and support community engagement initiatives.
Update Communication Strategy — Enhance the county communication strategy to be more representative of our population.
A Well-Planned, Maintained, and Growing Infrastructure
Strategic Priorities
Complete Asset Management Plan — Complete the MD’s asset management strategy so that Council can make informed decisions on the long-term infrastructure needs of the Municipal District of Taber. This involves determining what assets are in place, where they are located, and assessing the condition of the assets.
Long-term Financial Planning — Create a long-term financial strategy for the replacement of existing infrastructure and development of new infrastructure to support our growth into the future.

Fire Ban
Todays fire rating is Moderate
Current Fire Rating:
Moderate
A Fire Advisory is in Effect.
Due to current hot, dry conditions and continued dry weather in the forecast, the Municipal District of Taber has issued a Fire Advisory for all municipal boundaries, effective immediately and until further notice.
While the Fire Advisory is in effect, residents and visitors are advised that there is an elevated risk of wildfire.
Safe campfires are allowed on public land, in campgrounds, and on private land.
A fire permit must be obtained before burning. Apply for a fire permit online here.
Fire permits may be restricted or suspended.
Anyone conducting a controlled burn is urged to exercise extreme caution and closely monitor conditions at all times.
The Municipal District of Taber will continue to monitor weather and fire risk conditions and will adjust the advisory as necessary. The goal of the advisory is to raise public awareness of the increased fire danger, help protect people and property, and reduce the risk of costly emergency responses.
Last modified: July 29, 2026 at 10:00 a.m.

Fire Ban
Todays fire rating is Moderate
Current Fire Rating:
Moderate
A Fire Advisory is in Effect.
Due to current hot, dry conditions and continued dry weather in the forecast, the Municipal District of Taber has issued a Fire Advisory for all municipal boundaries, effective immediately and until further notice.
While the Fire Advisory is in effect, residents and visitors are advised that there is an elevated risk of wildfire.
Safe campfires are allowed on public land, in campgrounds, and on private land.
A fire permit must be obtained before burning. Apply for a fire permit online here.
Fire permits may be restricted or suspended.
Anyone conducting a controlled burn is urged to exercise extreme caution and closely monitor conditions at all times.
The Municipal District of Taber will continue to monitor weather and fire risk conditions and will adjust the advisory as necessary. The goal of the advisory is to raise public awareness of the increased fire danger, help protect people and property, and reduce the risk of costly emergency responses.
Last modified: July 29, 2026 at 10:00 a.m.
View the MD of Taber's Fire Services Bylaw No. 2013 or Fire Ban Implementation Policy below for insight into the types of Fire Bans issued.

Concession Rentals:
This family friendly, clean, well-maintained campground is within walking distance to local restaurants, Kneehill Historical Museum, and other amenities, Three Hills Campground is a convenient and comfortable place to enjoy the summer. Click here for more information on Ball Diamond Rentals .
Features:
47 Sites, camp concession (with non-commercial kitchen) available for rent, shower facilities, ball diamonds, play park, firewood available. Serviced and un-serviced lots available.

Area Campgrounds
Acme Campground
Walsh Avenue, Acme
403-352-0291
www.acme.ca/index.php/enjoying-acme/acme-campground
Located on the south end of Acme is Frank Fooks Memorial Park with a well treed campground, including 16 power/water 30 amp stalls, and on-site campground management. Within a short walking distance, there is a new washroom/shower facility.
Braconnier Dam
Hwy 21 South of Three Hills
www.kneehillcounty.com/2200/Braconnier-Dam
This small campground (3 acres) is located just off Highway 21 along with a natural draw, which has a small dammed water body. The waters here are not stocked due to the high pH levels in the water and are located on and owned by the adjacent landowner. The site comfortably allows for 10 stalls, which each have their own picnic tables and fire pits. There is also outhouses and a camp kitchen with municipal tap water.
Carbon Main and Carbon East Campgrounds
403-572-3244
http://villageofcarbon.com/attractions/campgrounds
Main Campground is located near downtown Carbon on Caradoc Avenue (Main Street) near the swimming pool, school and local amenities. East Campground is located along the 836 Highway (Rosebud Street) on the east edge of the village. Within short walking distance of the Main Campground, swimming pool and downtown Carbon.
Keiver’s Lake Campground
Hwy 583 and RR 26-0
403-443-7308
www.kneehillcounty.com/2198/Keivers-Lake-Campground
The popular Keiver’s Lake is located 1 mile south of Highway 583 on Range Road 26-0. The campground runs along the NE portion of the Lake with large old tree growth creating a picturesque site as well as providing shelter. With a full time Park Attendant on-site during the season, May 15 - September 30, there are over 50 campsites available; 25 marked, 25 random, 3 group sites, and 3 tent only sites.
Linden East Coulee Campground
Central Avenue and 5th Street NW
403-546-3888
www.linden.ca/index.php/visitor-information/campground
Spend time in the lovely East Coulee Campground where you can enjoy the quiet life of a small village on the prairies. Situated beside a stocked catch and release trout pond in a valley that intersects the village. Enjoy the variety of wildlife that migrates through on a regular basis. You can see muskrats, ducks, geese, deer and many others.
Starland Recreation Area
Highway 27, Morrin
403-772-3793
www.starlandcounty.com/sections/visiting-starland-county/starland-public-campgrounds
The Starland Recreation Area features 75 sites, nature trails, access to fishing, three baseball diamonds, a playground, outhouse toilets, fire pits, free firewood, drinking water, and a camp kitchen.
Swalwell Dam
West off Hwy 21 on Twp. Rd 30-2 then South on 24-4
403-443-7308
www.kneehillcounty.com/2199/Swalwell-Dam
Camping, Fishing, Day use May 15 - September 30
Swalwell campground located along the Swalwell Dam just South West of the Hamlet of Swalwell is a stocked dam for fishing. The site is comfortable allowing for 10 stalls, which each have their own picnic tables and fire pits. There are picnic tables, park benches, fire pits and day use sites as well as outhouses located here.
Three Hills Campground
1401 2nd Street North
403-443-1123
The Three Hills Campground is located on the east side of Town just off Secondary Road 583. 47 Sites, complete with camp concession stand, shower facilities, ball diamonds, and within walking distance to local restaurants and other amenities, the Three Hills campground it the perfect place to stay and play!!
Three Hills Golf Club and Campground
South of Highway 583 on RR 242
403-443-5065
www.threehillsgolfclub.ca
If you enjoy camping and golf you just found the perfect place. They offer large sites with power and water hookups as well as a dumping station. If it is one night, a weekend or the whole summer they will be able to accommodate you. If you would like to put a package together, please check out the stay and play section.
Tolman East Campground
East of Trochu on Highway 585
403-823-1749
www.albertaparks.ca/dry-island-buffalo-jump/information-facilities/camping/tolman-east
At the east campground, most sites are in open grassy fields and close together. There are some private, large sites surrounded by brush. This campground is located on the flood plain in the Red Deer River Valley. At the west campground, there are many large private sites surrounded with thick ground cover.
Torrington Village Campground
South side of Highway 27
403-443-5541
The Torrington Campground is located in an open field with gravel parking pads near restaurants and a small store.
Trochu Golf and Country Club and Campground
101 Devilder Avenue
403-442-2747
www.trochugolf.com
Stay at one of Trochu Golf Club’s campsites overlooking the coulee full of beautiful golf. Campsites are serviced with power and water available. The Town of Trochu has a sewer dump located at the UFA gas station available for use at no cost.
Trochu Lions Campground
235 Elevator Rd, Trochu
403-442-3061 or 403-304-7554
The campground has 38 full serviced lots, water, sewer, 30 amp power, fire pits and one dumping station. 11 of the lots have winter services available. Heated washrooms with hot and cold running water are on the grounds.
Entertainment is available in the form of, a large sandbox, two sets of horseshoe pits, three ball diamonds with shale infields, player dugouts and bleachers.
