Black Nugget Lake Campground
Nestled in the serene beauty of Beaver County and just a short drive from Tofield, Black Nugget Lake Campground offers a peaceful escape on grounds transformed from a former coal mine. This unique destination welcomes both seasoned campers and newcomers to enjoy its 90 diverse sites, catering to a range of camping styles from full-service to non-serviced, including tent and group sites.
Embrace outdoor activities like kayaking, birdwatching, fishing, and hiking around the picturesque lake. Enjoy our upgraded facilities, including renovated concession, improved washrooms, showers, and a revamped dump station, ensuring your stay is comfortable.
Black Nugget Lake, teeming with rainbow and tiger trout, invites anglers for fishing against a backdrop of breathtaking sunsets. Our day-use areas are perfect for picnicking or simply relaxing in lush surroundings. Planning your getaway? Note that reservations require a minimum two-day stay, extending to three days on long weekends, and we’re pet-friendly, allowing two pets per unit with a leash requirement. Rediscover nature’s tranquility at Black Nugget Lake Campground.
2026 Season
Black Nugget Lake Campground opens May 14 , through to September 28 .
Online booking will open at 9 a.m. on March 1st .
New for the 2026 season - Seasonal Sites!
Any off season inquiries please contact the Beaver County office at 780-663-3730.
Online Booking
Let's Camp! Booking Site
How to use our online booking site:
Seasonal Site Information & Booking
Seasonal Sites 23 through 32, shown in Orange
Make Black Nugget Your Summer Home!
New for the 2026 season, we’re excited to offer seasonal powered sites for those who want more than just a weekend getaway.
Sites 23–32 are now designated for seasonal stays, conveniently located near the playground and concession — close to the action, yet still surrounded by the beauty of the campground.
Set up once. Stay all season. Relax a little longer.
Seasonal campers are welcome to bring golf carts to make getting around even easier.
Why Go Seasonal?
✔ Set up once — no packing up every weekend
✔ More time to relax, fish, and enjoy the outdoors
✔ Convenient powered sites close to amenities
✔ Become part of a welcoming campground community
✔ Your own reliable summer retreat
More Information
Seasonal Rate: $3,500 (May 14 through September 28)
To inquire about a seasonal site please reach out to the Infrastructure team through our Contact Form or call the office at 780-663-3730 and speak to the Infrastructure team.
Day Use Rules, Regulations and Form
User of the Day Use areas at Beaver County Campgrounds are required to read the Rules and Regulations, and complete the Day Use Form.
Day Use Rules, Regulations and Form
Location
49117 RR 182
Black Nugget Lake Park is located between Tofield and Ryley, Highway 14 east 10 km, then south 11 km on RR 182.
15 minutes east of Tofield, 60 minutes east of Edmonton.
Reservation/Cancellation/Refund Policy
To provide for better management and visitor satisfaction Beaver County has implemented a policy for Reservations, Cancellations and Refunds.
The policy provides restrictions on over-booking and last minute cancellations resulting in more sites being available for other campers. The policy also ensures that the reservation holder is responsible for the actions of all-party members. Refunds will not be given for an eviction, vacating a campsite early, or for inclement weather.
The policy is based on practices which have been used in the past, and is based mainly on the refund policy established for Alberta Provincial Parks campgrounds.
To view a copy of the Reservation/Cancellation/Refund Policy click here .
Contact Us
For reservations see the Online Booking and Seasonal Site sections above.
For questions during May to September, call the Campground directly at 780-663-2421.
For off-season queries (October to April), contact infrastructure via our contact form or call 780-663-3730.

Camp Lake Park

Encircled by lush greenery and diverse wildlife, it's a paradise for those who love nature. Explore scenic trails, engage in birdwatching, or simply enjoy the peaceful surroundings. With modern amenities tailored for both seasoned campers and newcomers, whether you're in a tent or an RV, Camp Lake welcomes you.
Join us at Camp Lake Campground for a chance to connect with nature and create lasting memories. Plan your visit now and soak in the natural beauty of Beaver County.

Facilities
Feature Overview
Feature Overview
Find a Facility
You can find facilities in a number of different ways. You may utilize our search functionality located on the left side of the screen. You can search through all facilities and look for specific features or search through reservable facilities during the specific time of your event. Feel free to put in as much or as little information to meet your need.
View facilities on the map to quickly see their general locations, or you can view information on the listing screen and sort them in a way that best meets your need. Then, when you find what you are looking for, click on the facility for more information!
View Facility Events
If a facility has a public calendar, you can view it at the bottom of the facility’s page. The calendar will show any events that are taking place at the facility and you can click on the event for more information. If the facility contains any subfacilities, you will be able to select which ones you want to see directly on the main facility’s calendar. Sign up for iCal Updates in order to add events to your own personal calendars automatically!
Share Information with Your Friends
Quickly and easily share facility information with your friends using Facebook, Twitter, Google Plus, or Email.
Account Owner Features
As a site account owner, there are several features made available just to you:
Rate Facilities : Contribute to the website and help others by rating the facilities that you have been to.
Reserve Facilities : Book a facility online for your special event. Just fill out the form, make your payment (if applicable), and you’re done! You can even book the facility for recurring events if you need to.
Save Your Searches : If you search using the same criteria on a regular basis, save the search so that you don’t have to fill out the information each time.
Submit a Missing Facility : Is something missing from our list? Let us know if we have missed anything by sending us the name and any important details so that we can add it to the website.
Subscribe to iCal : Want to stay up to date on what is happening at your favorite facility? Subscribe to iCal and the events will be added to your personal calendar automatically!

Grande Cache Campground
Home
Tourism
Campgrounds & Day Use Areas
Grande Cache Campground
Grande Cache Campground
The Grande Cache Campground offers full-service RV or tent camping in a spectacular mountain setting.
Located within the Hamlet of Grande Cache, our campground has immediate access to baseball diamonds, hiking and multi-use trails, and the Grande Cache Golf & Country Club. The campground is operated by Grande Cache, MD of Greenview and is open May long weekend until October (weather permitting).
Facility Features:
1 RV per site
77 large treed sites (56 full-service, 21 partial-service, 1 open tenting area)
All sites include a picnic table
Laundry facilities
Shower and washroom facilities
Lit roadways
Limited Wifi near the office
Resources
Grande Cache Campground Brochure
Grande Cache Campground Map
Contact Information:
Phone: 780-827-2404
Office Hours: 8:30 am – 7:00 pm (Note: Coins for laundry & payment for firewood during office hours only)
Email: GCCamp@mdgreenview.ab.ca
Find us – Driving Directions:
From Hinton, head north on Highway 40. Once in town, take the second right off Highway 40 onto Shand Avenue.
From Grande Prairie, take Highway 40 south. Take your first left off Highway 40 onto Shand Avenue as you arrive in Grande Cache.
From Highway 40, turn east on Shand Avenue, turn left on 104 Avenue and continue onto Memorial Drive. Turn right at the Campground sign.
Close to the ball diamonds & Grande Cache Golf & Country Club
Grande Cache Campground
10401 Memorial Drive | Access Road to the Campground SW 1/4 3 57 8 W6
PO Box 1079 | Valleyview, AB | T0H 3N0
2026 Fee Schedule:
Full-service (power, water, sewer & one firewood bundle): $ 50.00 per night
Partial-service (power, water & one firewood bundle): $ 45.00 per night
Monthly site rate (full service. Availability determines upon season opening): $ 1,100.00 per month (contact for limited availability)
Open Tent Area: $ 25.00 per night
Firewood: $ 20.00 per wheelbarrow load
Cook Shack Rental: $100.00 per day
Shower/washroom facilities: Free of charge
Laundry facilities: Coin-operated
Online Booking Information:
Online Reservations will be available beginning April 1, 2026, at 10:00 am
Grande Cache Campground will open on May 15, 2026, at 9:00 am
Grande Cache Campground will close for reservations and bookings on October 13, 2026 (weather permitting)
Self-registration is available at the Grande Cache Campground
TO BOOK ONLINE: https://letscamp.ca/camps/gccampground (online booking link will be active April 1, 2026 at 10:00 am)
Campground Reservation Procedures:
You will require a VISA/MC/AMEX and a valid email address (so you can receive your electronic receipt and reservation confirmation).
Cancellations:
“No Shows” will not be refunded under any circumstances.
If you wish to cancel your online reservation and receive a refund, we require a minimum of 3 business days’ notice (with noon being the starting time). All cancellations will be subject to the booking fee and a one-night non-refundable deposit. There will be no exceptions, regardless of the circumstances, so please see the examples below.
Example 1: You have a reservation for a long weekend (Friday, Saturday, and Sunday nights). On Tuesday, you have a family emergency, and you know that you will not be able to go camping that weekend. If you contact the Grande Cache Campground by telephone or email before Tuesday at noon, you will qualify for a refund. This allows 3 complete business days before the noon check-in time at the campground on Friday. If you call at any time after 12 noon on Tuesday, you will not receive any refund. No exceptions.
Example 2: You have a reservation that starts next Tuesday. On Thursday, you decide that you have to cancel your reservation. If you contact the Grande Cache Campground by telephone or email before Thursday at noon, you will qualify for a refund. This allows for 3 business days’ notice (Friday, Monday, and Tuesday) before the noon check-in on Tuesday. If you call at any time after 12 noon on Thursday, you will not receive any refund. No exceptions.
Information & Campground Procedures:
Length of Stay Policy:
Check-in time 2:00 pm
Check-out time 11:00 am
All campers must register prior to parking their RV unit or setting up their tent
Office hours are posted on the building
Site checks are done daily by staff
Camp Permit Policy
No one under 18 years of age will be granted a camping permit
Cleanliness
Please keep your campsite clean at all times
Remember to store all food in a safe place. Do not leave any food, empty cans/bottles, garbage, dog food, or bear attractants lying around.
Remember to keep BBQs clean.
A bottle/can recycle bin is located across from the Wood Shed
Quiet Time
Quiet time 11:00 p.m. to 9:00 a.m. Quiet time is strictly enforced, and noise will not be tolerated during these hours. Please respect other campers.
Campfires
Due to the risk of disease and infestation from outside firewood sources, the Grande Cache Campground is restricting campers from bringing their own firewood on site. The Grande Cache Campground sells locally sourced firewood on-site at a cost of $20.00 per wheelbarrow load that can be purchased and used in our fire pits. We thank you for your diligence in protecting our forests and respecting our campground rules.
Campfires in designated fire pits only
No open or unattended fires
Fireworks are not allowed
Pets
All pets must be on a leash at all times
You are required to clean up after your pet
Grey Water
DO NOT drain grey water into the trees or bush, work areas or grass
The sewage dump is located in front of the Operations Office at 9706 Shand Avenue or at the full-service sites
Shower, Washroom, and Laundry Facilities
Located beside the main Campground Office
Shower and washroom facilities are free of charge for registered campers only
Washers and dryers are coin-operated. Change is available during office hours only
Please keep the facilities clean for fellow campers
Self Registration & phone registration is available by contacting the Campground Office
Self-registration is for one night only after office hours ONLY.
If you do not have cash, please leave your cell number to process a credit card payment. We do not accept personal cheques.
Please fill out the registration form located in the green mailbox. Must register within 30 minutes of arriving at the site. Place the white copy of the registration with your payment inside the envelope and take the yellow copy for your records. Drop the sealed envelope in the slot.
Cook House and Day Use Area
Registered campers can book the Cook House through the Campground Office
Day use area is located in the centre of the campground and is for all campground users
Please keep your campsite clean at all times. Remember to store all food in a safe place. Do not leave any food, empty cans/bottles, garbage, dog food, or bear attractants lying around
ATV Use
ATVs are not permitted to be operated in the campground.
Liquor
Alcoholic beverages are permitted in registered campsites only.
Damage Policy
Liability for loss or damage to personal property or personal injury while on campground property is solely the responsibility of occupants and guests.
Failure to observe the above rules may be grounds for eviction.

Corporate Services
Home
Departments
Corporate Services
Corporate Services Department
The Corporate Services department at Greenview plays a vital role in supporting the organization’s operations, ensuring financial stability, transparency, and effective resource management. Through key areas such as Finance, Asset Management, Legislative Services, Procurement, Human Resources, and Information Systems, Corporate Services provides the infrastructure for sound financial practices, legal compliance, responsible procurement, and employee support. This department also upholds Greenview’s commitment to transparent governance, sustainable asset management, and the technology solutions needed to enhance productivity and service delivery across all municipal functions.
Accounting & Reporting
The Accounting and Reporting department manages the financial operations and service delivery that support Greenview’s fiscal integrity and public accountability. In accordance with the Municipal Government Act (MGA), this department oversees the administration of taxation, financial statements, accounts payable, and utility billing, ensuring compliance with legislative requirements and alignment with Council-approved budgets and business plans.
This department provides essential support to all departments and residents by facilitating accurate financial reporting, timely vendor payments, and reliable billing services. Its responsibilities encompass the issuance of tax certificates and searches, administration of the Tax Installment Payment Plan (TIPP), processing of name and mailing address changes, and coordination of tax payment options. Through the diligent execution of these services, the department ensures Greenview maintains the financial infrastructure necessary to sustain ongoing and newly introduced programs and initiatives.
Budget and Financial Planning
The Budget and Financial Planning department is tasked with planning and managing the development and approval of operating and capital budgets in accordance with the Municipal Government Act (MGA). This department supports all departments and residents by ensuring Greenview possesses the financial resources necessary to sustain ongoing and newly introduced programs and initiatives.
Its responsibilities encompass accounting for tangible capital assets, asset retirement obligations, long-term financing strategies, reserve fund management, and debt oversight. Through the efficient allocation of funds, accurate forecasting of financial requirements, and alignment of expenditures with strategic objectives, the department upholds fiscal integrity, accountability, and transparency in managing public finances—enabling Greenview to maintain fiscal responsibility and achieve its organizational goals.
Legislative Services
Legislative Services supports relationships among Greenview Council, Administration, and Greenview ratepayers. Legislative Services preserves the integrity of the democratic process by ensuring open and transparent government through the development of sound practices and systems for supporting effective decision-making by Council. This includes ensuring that all activities of Greenview are conducted within legislative provisions respecting the roles and responsibilities of local government as set out in the MGA, the Local Authorities Election Act and the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act.
Procurement
Procurement collaborates and supports departments to meet their purchasing and procurement needs in a methodology of fair, cost-effective, equitable, open, and transparent manner.
Human Resources
The Human Resources team is committed to supporting all employees, including Management and the Senior Leadership Team, with all their individual, team and department goals and recruitment efforts while aiming to promote a positive and healthy work environment at Greenview. The Human Resources team also includes dedicated Health and Safety professionals who provide training, support, and promotion of an employee-driven, values-based safety culture.
Information Systems
The Information Systems team provides support in all forms of technology. They work hard to support all Greenview employees and elected officials and provide technical assistance for hardware and software to ensure that all employees have the necessary tools to do their jobs effectively and efficiently.

Taxes
Home
Departments
Corporate Services
Taxes
Non-residential taxes are due June 30, 2026, and residential/farmland taxes are due November 16, 2026. Greenview strives to send out tax notices in May of each year.
2026 Notice of Mailing
If you have not received a tax notice by June 1, please contact the Finance Coordinator, Taxation & Assessment at 780.524.7600 or select contact us at the bottom of the page to send an email message, as you are liable to pay your taxes even if a notice has not been received.
An 8% penalty is applied to unpaid current taxes after June 30, 2026, for non-residential/commercial properties, and after November 16, 2026, for residential/farmland properties, each year. A further 10% penalty is applied to all outstanding taxes on January 1st of each year. Any tax account that is one year in arrears receives an additional 18% penalty. Taxes that remain unpaid at the beginning of the second calendar year following the year in which the tax notice is mailed will result in a tax notification being registered on their title. If the taxes still remain unpaid one year after that, by legislation, the property will be put up for tax recovery public auction by the municipality.
Example: 2009 taxes unpaid by January 1, 2011 tax notification registered on the title. January 1, 2012, taxes still unpaid tax recovery public auction.
Education Property Taxes*
In Alberta, education is a provincial program. The taxes that fund the program are raised and distributed on a provincial basis. Education property tax dollars are pooled in the Alberta School Foundation Fund and then allocated among school boards throughout the province.
This system of pooling taxes from all municipalities ensures that funds are available to provide all students with a standard level of education, no matter where they live.
Each year the province calculates the amount that every Alberta municipality must contribute towards the public education system. The calculation is based on a formula that takes into account the equalized assessment in each municipality and the provincial uniform education property tax rate.
The province notifies municipalities of the amount of education taxes they are required to collect. Each municipality then establishes a local education property tax rate. This tax rate is calculated by dividing the required amount by the municipality’s current taxable assessment.
The municipality then applies its local education tax rate to the assessed value of each property to determine the amount of education taxes each property owner is required to pay for the year. The education property tax is included on the annual Combined Property Assessment and Tax notice that is sent to property owners. The education tax dollars are collected from the ratepayers and sent to the province or to a separate school board. All separate school boards in the province have “opted out” of the Alberta School Foundation Fund, which means they requisition and collect property tax money from the municipalities directly.
Commonly Asked Questions *
Does everyone pay the education property tax?
All property owners pay the education property tax. People who rent or lease property contribute indirectly through their monthly rent or lease payments. As the education system benefits all Albertans, people without children in school also pay the education property tax.
Do seniors have to pay the education property tax?
Seniors who own property must pay the education property tax, however there are a number of options which may provide assistance.
The Government of Alberta has established the Seniors Property Tax Deferral Program which allows eligible senior homeowners to defer all or part of their property taxes through a low-interest home equity loan with the Alberta government. The Government of Alberta then pays the property taxes on behalf of the eligible home owner. The loan does not have to be repaid until the property is sold or sooner if the home owner chooses.
The Government of Alberta also provides financial assistance to low-income seniors through the Alberta Seniors Benefit. The Alberta Seniors Benefit provides monthly cash benefits, which can help seniors with their property taxes or other expenses. It provides support in addition to the federal benefits received including Old Age Security and Guaranteed Income Supplement.
For more information about the Alberta Education Property Tax call toll free by dialing 310.0000 and then 780-422-7125 .
Seniors can contact Alberta Seniors toll-free at 1-877-644-9992 or visit their website for more information on:
Seniors Property Tax Deferral Program ,
Alberta Seniors Benefit ,
or other provincial programs and services for seniors.
* Source : The Government of Alberta

Tax Payment Options
Home
Departments
Corporate Services
Tax Payment Options
The Tax Installment Payment Plan (TIPP) offers MD of Greenview taxpayers a convenient plan that enables you to pay your property tax in 12 monthly payments (January-December) instead of one annual payment. Click here to enroll for TIPP.
Mail
Send a cheque or money order (please do not send cash) to:
Municipal District of Greenview No. 16
Box 1079
Valleyview, AB T0H 3N0
Please record your tax roll number, customer number or account number on the cheque and enclose the return portion of your bill. For tax payments the envelope must be postmarked by Canada Post on or before the due date, otherwise, late payment penalties will be added.
Post-Dated Cheques
Post-dated cheques are also accepted by the municipality. The cheques must be dated for the due date or earlier to avoid penalty. Please record your roll number or customer number on the cheque and enclose the return portion of your bill with payment.
Credit Card
Go to PaySimply.ca
Click on Municipalities
Type in Greenview
Choose what you would like to pay (Taxes, Utilities, AR)
Following this, you will be asked to enter your email address, the account holder’s name, the account number (numerical input only), and the payment amount
Next, enter your credit card information
Once processed, you will be given a transaction number, and a receipt will be emailed to you from PaySimply
Greenview does not accept e-transfers
In-Person
Our friendly staff would be happy to assist you at the following locations:
Valleyview Administration Office
4806 – 36 Avenue [View Map]
PO Box 1079, Valleyview, AB T0H 3N0
Phone: 780.524.7600
Toll Free: 1.888.524.7601
24/7 Dispatch: 1.866.524.7608
Fax: 780.524.4307
Office Hours: 8:00 a.m. – 4:30 p.m.
(Closed for Lunch from Noon – 1 p.m.)
Grovedale Public Service Building
70075 Range Road 64, Lot 3 [View Map]
PO Box 1079, Valleyview, AB T0H 3N0
Phone: 780.539.0863
Fax: 780.539.1875
Office Hours: 8:00 a.m. – 4:30 p.m.
(Closed for Lunch from Noon – 1 p.m.)
Note: Cash payments are not accepted at this location
DeBolt Public Service Building
1115 Township Road 721A [View Map]
PO Box 1079 Valleyview, AB T0H 3N0
Phone: 780.957.3740
Fax: 780.957.3796
Office Hours: 8:00 a.m. – 4:30 p.m.
(Closed for Lunch from Noon – 1 p.m.)
Note: Cash payments are not accepted at this location
Grande Cache Public Service Building
10002 Shand Avenue
PO Box 1079, Valleyview, AB T0H 3N0
Phone: 780.827.3362
Fax: 780.827.2406
Office Hours: 8:00 a.m. – 4:30 p.m.
(Closed for Lunch from Noon – 1 p.m.)
Another option is to make your tax payment at any financial institution. Please take your tax notice with you.
Banking Online/Tele-Banking
You may also choose to set up the MD as one of your online banking payees; you will have three accounts to choose from: accounts receivable, taxes and utilities.

Recreation Services
Home
Departments
Recreation Services
Recreation Services Department
Greenview Recreation Services Department manages the following indoor recreation facilities (Grande Cache Recreation Centre & the Greenview Regional Multiplex) and outdoor recreation spaces within the MD of Greenview.
Recreation Services also facilitates high quality programs and services for all ages to enhance the health, quality of life, and wellbeing of residents.
Contact Information
Grande Cache Recreation Centre
Phone: 780-827-2446
Facebook: Grande Cache Recreation Centre
Greenview Regional Multiplex
Phone: 780-524-4097
Email: grminfo@mdgreenview.ab.ca

Grande Cache Community Bus

Grande Cache Recreation Centre
The Grande Cache Recreation Centre is home to a first-class aquatic centre, hockey arena, curling rink, fitness centre, climbing cave, meeting and party rooms, and a variety of great sport, fitness and community programs for all ages. Adjacent to the facility is Central Park, which features a Spray Park, picnic tables, paved walking paths and an outdoor green gym.
Learn More
Greenview Regional Multiplex
The Greenview Regional Multiplex is an 82042 sq ft recreational facility in the heart of the MD of Greenview serving approximately 7000 people in the region. A family friendly multiuse facility with an Aquatic Centre, Fitness Centre, Fieldhouse, Walking Track, Childmind Centre, Dance Studios, Commercial Kitchen, Party Room, and Concession .
Learn More
Campgrounds & Day Use Areas
Explore Greenview’s scenic campgrounds and day-use areas, perfect for outdoor activities, family gatherings, and relaxation. This page provides details on locations, amenities, and reservation information.
Learn More
Playgrounds & Spray Parks
Discover safe, family-friendly playgrounds and spray parks across Greenview, offering fun and engaging outdoor spaces for children and families to enjoy.
Learn More
Arenas & Curling Rinks
Access Greenview’s arenas and curling rinks for activities like skating, hockey, and curling. These facilities provide residents with spaces for sports, recreation, and community events.
Learn More
Community Bus Services
Learn about Greenview’s community bus services, which offer accessible and convenient transportation options for residents, including routes for in-town and regional travel

Expand All
Bellis Beach
Location: Approximately 25 km east of Smoky Lake and 2 km south of Bellis turn-off
24 campsites
First-Come, First-Served
Playground area
Day-use and picnic area
Lake stocked rainbow trout
Gasoline engine watercraft are restricted in this protected area
Fees: $25.00/ night
View: How to Pay for Your Campsite
Campground Open:
May 1 to October 31
Campground Manager: Smoky Lake County 780-650-1800
Hanmore Lake
Location: There are campgrounds located on both the east side and far west side of the lake.
East Campground:
Location: Approximately 20 km north of the Town of Smoky Lake on HWY 855, turn west of TWP RD 612 then north on RGE RD 174.
16 campsites and 1 large group site
Main beach area with swimming docks
Day-use and picnic area with playground
Public boat launch
Firewood and ice available for purchase
Kayak & paddle board rentals
Pet friendly
No power, water or sewer services
Fees:
$25.00/ night
Reserve your spot through: https://letscamp.ca/
Campground Open: May 14 to October 4
Campground Manager: Jackie 780-
656-6580
West Campground:
Location: Approximately 25 km north of Smoky Lake on HWY 855, turn west on TWP RD 612, then winding north on RGE RD 180
39 campsites
Smaller beach/ swimming area
Small beach and playground
Boat launch
Boat trailer parking available
Firewood and ice available for purchase
Kayak & paddle board rentals
Pet friendly
No power, water or sewer services
Fees: $25.00/ night
Reserve your spot through:
https://letscamp.ca/
Campground Open: May 14 to October 4
Campground Manager: Jackie 780-
656-6580
Island Lake
Location: Approximately 28 km north of the Town of Smoky Lake
9 campsites
Firewood available for purchase
Pet friendly
No power, water or sewer services
Fees: $25.00/ night
Reserve your spot through : https://letscamp.ca/
Campground Open: May 15 to October 4
Campground Manager: Jackie 780-656-6580
Kaduk Lake
Location: Approximately 17 km from Highway 28
at the Bellis turnoff, or roughly 13 km from Bellis, AB
11 campsites
First-Come, First-Served
Day-use and picnic area
Lake is best suited to small craft like canoes, kayaks and paddle boats
Fees: $25.00/ night
View: How to Pay for Your Campsite
Campground Open: May 1 to October 31
Campground Manager: Smoky Lake County 780-650-1800
Mons Lake
Location: Approximately 6.5 km east and 3.2 km north of the Town of Smoky Lake
8 campsites
First-Come, First-Served
2 playground areas
Day-use area with swimming docks
Public boat launch at day-use area
Fees:
$25.00/ night
View: How to Pay for Your Campsite
Campground Open: May 1 to October 31
Campground Manager: Smoky Lake County 780-650-1800
Smoky Lake RV Park
The Smoky Lake RV Park is located in Smoky Lake, behind the Smoky Lake Agricultural Complex. It offers spacious stalls, perfect for RV units and tents, with trees surrounding and in between each site.
For more information visit: Camping | smokylakeagsociety
Shemeluk Lake
Location: Approximately 6.5 km east and 3.2 km north of the Town of Smoky Lake
Day-use and picnic area
Stocked with rainbow trout
Gasoline engine watercraft are restricted
Campground Manager: Smoky Lake County 780-650-1800

Smoky Lake County Council adopted the 2026-2029 Strategic Plan in May of 2026 identifying 5 strategic priorities.
Priority 1: Regional Collaboration & Modernization
Priority 2: Service Delivery & Community Wellbeing
Priority 3: Asset Management & Infrastructure Sustainability
Priority 4: Economic Development & Financial Sustainability
Priority 5: Workforce Development & Succession Planning

Campground Manager: Smoky Lake County 780-650-1800
Hanmore Lake
Location: There are campgrounds located on both the east side and far west side of the lake.
East Campground:
Location: Approximately 20 km north of the Town of Smoky Lake on HWY 855, turn west of TWP RD 612 then north on RGE RD 174.
16 campsites and 1 large group site
Main beach area with swimming docks
Day-use and picnic area with playground
Public boat launch
Firewood and ice available for purchase
Kayak & paddle board rentals
Pet friendly
No power, water or sewer services
Fees:

656-6580

39 campsites
Smaller beach/ swimming area
Small beach and playground
Boat launch
Boat trailer parking available
Firewood and ice available for purchase
Kayak & paddle board rentals
Pet friendly
No power, water or sewer services
Fees: $25.00/ night
Reserve your spot through:
https://letscamp.ca/
Campground Open: May 14 to October 4
Campground Manager: Jackie 780-

Island Lake
Location: Approximately 28 km north of the Town of Smoky Lake
9 campsites

Pet friendly

Fees: $25.00/ night
Reserve your spot through : https://letscamp.ca/
Campground Open: May 15 to October 4
Campground Manager: Jackie 780-656-6580

at the Bellis turnoff, or roughly 13 km from Bellis, AB
11 campsites
First-Come, First-Served
Day-use and picnic area
Lake is best suited to small craft like canoes, kayaks and paddle boats
Fees: $25.00/ night
View: How to Pay for Your Campsite
Campground Open: May 1 to October 31
Campground Manager: Smoky Lake County 780-650-1800

2 playground areas

Public boat launch at day-use area
Fees:

View: How to Pay for Your Campsite

The Smoky Lake RV Park is located in Smoky Lake, behind the Smoky Lake Agricultural Complex. It offers spacious stalls, perfect for RV units and tents, with trees surrounding and in between each site.
For more information visit: Camping | smokylakeagsociety

Priority 2: Service Delivery & Community Wellbeing
Priority 3: Asset Management & Infrastructure Sustainability
Priority 4: Economic Development & Financial Sustainability
Priority 5: Workforce Development & Succession Planning

Camping Season
May 8 to September 6, 2026:
Chickenhill M.D. Park
Cold Lake M.D. Park
Crane Lake East/West M.D. Parks
Ethel Lake M.D. Park
French Bay M.D. Park
Minnie Lake East/West M.D. Parks
Pelican Point M.D. Park
Wolf Lake M.D. Park
May 1 to September 30, 2026:
Muriel Lake M.D. Park
Vezeau Beach M.D. Park
Reservations for 2026 Camping Season
Please stay tuned to this page for updates or letscamp.ca
Stays of one week or more begin March 30, 2026. All other reservations open April 1.
Campground rates and reservation website addresses may be subject to change. All prices are subject to GST and site fees.
Seasonal Camping is now available for Muriel Lake M.D. Park. Set up once, and stay all summer May 1 – September 30).
Monthly cabin rental available at Vezeau Beach M.D. Park. Please call 780-826-2245.
Cancellation Policy
In the event that you have to cancel your reservation, please provide at least 72 hours notice, prior to your expected check-in. One night's stay will be deducted from your camping fees for full or partial cancellations.
Failure to notify the campground park attendant or manage your booking online within 72 hours prior to check-in will result in the loss of your entire camping fee.
Rules and Regulations
No person shall interfere with the rights of others to the quiet and peaceful enjoyment of the park.
If generators are needed, please refrain from running your generators continuously throughout the day.
There will be zero tolerance for excessive noise from 11 p.m. to 7 a.m.
Park guests are expected to maintain clean sites. Please use garbage bins for waste - not fire pits. Campsites left in an unacceptable condition may result in a fine of $200 - $400.
Alcohol is not allowed off of your assigned campsite at any time.
Cannabis is not allowed off of your assigned campsite at any time.
All dogs must be leashed AT ALL TIMES. Dogs are not allowed on the beach AT ANY TIME. Cleaning up after your pets is mandatory.
The swimming and playground areas are NOT supervised. Use at your own risk.
Fireworks are prohibited in all M.D. Parks.
OHVs are prohibited inside the park ( except Pelican Point) .
For further rules and regulations please see
B
ylaw 1812
and
B
ylaw 1864
.
Chickenhill Lake
Chickenhill Lake M.D. Park
This little gem has 29, 30-amp powered sites. Grab a lakefront spot at Chickenhill Lake M.D. Park for great views of the sunset or set up in one of the forested sites to enjoy private, treed sites. If you’re looking for a calm and quiet lake to enjoy an afternoon in your canoe or on your paddleboard, look no further! Remember to bring your volleyball — the beach court here is full of soft sand, perfect for a day of friendly competition!
Rural Address: 59314 RGE RD 482.
How to get here: south of Hwy. 28 (at Glendon intersection) on Hwy. 882 (Rge. Rd. 484) for 6.4 km, east on Twp. Rd. 594 for 3.3 km, and then south on Rge. Rd. 482 for one km. From St. Paul go north on Hwy. 881 and east on Twp. Rd. 594 for 28.9 km.
Online reservations open for bookings of a week or more on March 30 at 8:30 a.m. General reservations open April 1 at 8:30 a.m. Park opens May 8, 2026.
Book online here
Cold Lake
Cold Lake M.D. Park
NEW IN 2026 – Our friendly staff will greet you at the new park office and gate.
From lakefront sites to walk-up tent sites, the Cold Lake M.D. Park offers 145 power and 14 non-powered sites. There is also potable water (including RV fill), flush toilets, coin-operated showers, and laundry on site. Find snacks, cold treats, and ice at our onsite store. Registered guests also have access to the boat launch located on the north end of the campground.
This campground provides a great adventure base camp. Take a short five minute walk to Kinosoo Beach and enjoy amenities such as a concession, multiple ice cream vendors, water sport rentals, basketball and volleyball courts, and the lakeside splash park.
Are you looking for a unique place to hold a celebration or private event? Check out our new picnic shelter, available for half-day or full-day rentals.
Located at: 2301-1 Ave. in Cold Lake.
Online reservations open for bookings of a week or more on March 30 at 8:30 a.m. General reservations open April 1 at 8:30 a.m. Park opens May 8, 2026.
Book online here
French Bay on Cold Lake M.D. Park
Camping at French Bay M.D. Park is like a nostalgic time machine, whisking you back to the good old days of unplugged adventures, while having modern comforts just a hop, skip, and a jump away! French Bay offers 10 non-power sites, a boat launch at the upper sites (use dependent on lake levels), a day use beach area, and swimming at the lower campsite. Non-potable water is available via hand pump.
Looking for adventure? Check out the 60-foot-tall Aerial Adventure Park or Target Golf located minutes away at Kinosoo Ridge Resort.
Rural Address: #2 63218 RGE RD 411.
How to get here: located 15 km northeast of Cold Lake, one km south of Kinosoo Ridge Resort, on the southeast shore of Cold Lake.
Online reservations open for bookings of a week or more on March 30 at 8:30 a.m. General reservations open April 1 at 8:30 a.m. Park opens May 8, 2026.
Book online here
Crane Lake
Crane Lake M.D. Park
Where the lake and forest meet, you’ll find a relaxing atmosphere at Crane Lake M.D. Park East. With 29, 30-amp power sites, hand pump for non-potable water, beach, and playground, this a great getaway for the whole family.
At Crane Lake M.D. Park West, you are never far from the lake! This campground offers 23, 30-amp power sites, a large beach, boat mooring, camp kitchen, and non-potable water. This clear lake is enjoyed by anglers, water sports enthusiasts, and swimmers alike!
East Side Rural Address: 64005 RGE RD 443.
West Side Rural Address: 64002 RGE RD 444.
How to get here: located 25 km west of Cold Lake along
Hwy. 55, five km north on Rge. Rd. 444.
Online reservations open for bookings of a week or more on March 30 at 8:30 a.m. General reservations open April 1 at 8:30 a.m. Park opens May 8, 2026.
Book online here
Ethel Lake
Ethel Lake M.D. Park
With only 11 non-power sites, Ethel Lake M.D. Park may be small, but it has a lot to keep you and your family occupied for a day or a week. Whether you have a pontoon or a kayak, it’s a great lake to spend the day on. After dinner, try your aim at the horseshoe pits.
Rural Address: 64232 RGE RD 431.
How to get here: located eight km west on Hwy. 55 and 10 km north on Hwy. 897.
Online reservations open for bookings of a week or more on March 30 at 8:30 a.m. General reservations open April 1 at 8:30 a.m. Park opens May 8, 2026.
Book online here
Minnie Lake
Minnie Lake M.D. Parks
Minnie Lake M.D. Park East offers an amazing getaway with 11, 30-amp power sites. Everything you need is here including, a day use picnic area, change rooms, beach with swimming area, diving platform, frisbee golf, and volleyball court. Want to rent a paddle board or feeling a little snacky? Come check out the store!
At Minnie Lake M.D. Park West, you’ll find seven large 30-amp power sites — the perfect venue for a family reunion! You’ll also find a boat launch and dock. This picturesque small lake is great for a variety of water activities.
East Side Rural Address: #17 61219 RGE RD 482.
West Side Rural Address: #45 61219 RGE RD 482.
How to get here: located five minutes northeast of Glendon, north off Hwy. 660.
Online reservations open for bookings of a week or more on March 30 at 8:30 a.m. General reservations open April 1 at 8:30 a.m. Park opens May 8, 2026.
Book online here
Moose Lake
Pelican Point on Moose Lake M.D. Park
Bring your quad or side-by-side to the M.D.’s Pelican Point campground for a trip full of exploring and fun! All 61 non-power individual sites are OHV friendly. Coming with a group of friends? Reserve one of our two large group sites. Check out the sand dunes outside of the park or hop on the Iron Horse Trail to explore the region.
Looking for a more tranquil experience? Take a walk through the forest and find a treasure trove of berries!
Remember to bring your fishing rod! Cast a line and hook a variety of fish including pike, walleye, and perch. Be sure to review the Alberta Guide to Sportfishing Regulations before reeling in your next big fish story.
Full regulations about OHV use within the park are posted here
.
Rural Address: 61015 RGE RD 474.
How to get here: located two km north of Bonnyville on Hwy. 41, 16 km west on Hwy. 660 and 6.5 km south on Rge. Rd. 474 OR one km north of Glendon, 10 km east on Hwy. 660 and 6.5 km south.
Online reservations open for bookings of a week or more on March 30 at 8:30 a.m. General reservations open April 1 at 8:30 a.m. Park opens May 8, 2026.
Book online here
Vezeau Beach on Moose Lake M.D. Park
Looking for a summer at the lake? Vezeau Beach M.D. Park has it all! This park offers 23 full-service sites (non-potable water) plus three power-only sites on the south shore of Moose Lake. Enjoy the convenience of having coin-operated laundry facilities and showers within walking distance. Head out for a day on the water using our two-lane boat launch with 15-boat slip dock. Kids can find hours of fun waiting for them at the playground and jumping pillow or by borrowing one of the outdoor games.
Spend an afternoon taking on the 18-hole course at the Bonnyville Golf & Country Club, located across the road. Bring your bike or favourite walking shoes and check out the extensive Moose Lake trail system.
When you check in at the Visitor Information & Interpretive Centre at the Shaw House, treat yourself to some delicious ice cream and a souvenir crafted by our talented local artisans!
No camper or tent? No problem! We have a cabin available for monthly bookings! The rental includes power, non-potable water, and a three-piece washroom. Bring your own bedding and linens. Please call 780-826-2245 to book your cabin adventure!
NEW THIS YEAR – The Shaw House is now a licenced facility. Enjoy a locally brewed beverage on the outdoor patio.
Rural Address: #1 46300 TWP RD 611.
How to get here : located five km west of Bonnyville on Hwy. 28
Online reservations open for bookings of a week or more on March 30 at 8:30 a.m. General reservations open April 1 at 8:30 a.m. Park opens May 1, 2026.
Book online here
Muriel Lake
Muriel Lake M.D. Park
With 54, 30-amp power, 39 non-power, and two non-power group areas, Muriel Lake is one of the M.D.’s largest campgrounds.
Featuring 13 kilometres of hiking and biking trails, baseball diamonds, two playgrounds, volleyball court, onsite store, and day use lookout area, this is the perfect play and stay destination! The campground also offers running non-potable water, barrier-free accessible washrooms, showers, and coin laundry.
Get a summer full of camping by booking one of our 20 seasonal sites. Set up your camper once and your getaway will always be ready for you from May 1 to September 30.
EVENTS - To see all events click here.
2026CLAIR – Use this promo code to receive 10% off your stay at Muriel Lake M.D. Park during the Cold Lake Air Show on July 18 and 19, 2026!
Rural Address: 60304 RGE RD 452.
How to get here : located 12 km east off Hwy. 28 (just before the Town of Bonnyville) on Twp. Rd. 610 and six km south on Rge. Rd. 452 (watch for signs).
Online reservations open for bookings of a week or more on March 30 at 8:30 a.m. General reservations open April 1 at 8:30 a.m. Park opens May 1, 2026.
Book online here
Wolf Lake
Wolf Lake M.D. Park
Wolf Lake M.D. Park has 59 non-power sites tucked away in the boreal forest, offering the best place to unplug, unwind, and relax.
Some of the best walleye fishing in the M.D. is here. Make sure you check the Alberta Guide to Sportfishing Regulations and get your walleye tags at mywildalberta.ca .
Non-potable water is available via hand pump.
DID YOU KNOW – Wolf Lake is a birdwatchers paradise! There are almost 300 species of birds in our region, and a lot of them fly over this lake. We fall in the transition zone between Alberta’s aspen parkland and the northern boreal forest.
Rural Address: 65014 RGE RD 475.
How to get here: located 20 km north of Bonnyville on Hwy. 41, 15 km west on Hwy. 55 and 30 km north on Rge. Rd. 475.
Online reservations open for bookings of a week or more on March 30 at 8:30 a.m. General reservations open April 1 at 8:30 a.m. Park opens May 8, 2026.
Book Online
Reservations are strongly recommended for all campgrounds. Campground rates, site details may be subject to change.

BYLAW NO. 1864
A BYLAW OF THE MUNICIPAL DISTRICT OF BONNYVILLE NO. 87, IN THE
PROVINCE OF ALBERTA TO PROVIDE FOR THE CONTROL AND OPERATION OF
PARKS AND CAMPGROUNDS UNDER THE JURISDICTION OF THE MUNICIPALITY
HEREBY CITED AS THE PARKS AND CAMPGROUND BYLAW.
WHEREAS, under the provisions of the Municipal Government Act, R.S.A 2000, Chapter M-26,
and amendments thereto, a Council’s power to pass a bylaw includes a power to amend or repeal
a bylaw;
AND WHEREAS, the Municipal Government Act, Chapter M-26, R.S.A. 2000 grants authority to
Council to pass bylaws with respect to the safety, health and welfare of people and the protection
of people and property;
AND WHEREAS, Council of the Municipal District of Bonnyville No. 87 has established public
parks and campgrounds;
AND WHEREAS, Council of the Municipal District of Bonnyville No. 87 wishes to establish rules
and regulations for the control and operation of its public parks and campgrounds;
NOW THEREFORE, the Council of the Municipal District of Bonnyville No. 87, duly assembled
in the Province of Alberta, hereby enacts the following:
1 DEFINITIONS
1.1 Words in the singular shall include the plural or vice versa whenever the context so
requires.
1.2 In this Bylaw the following definitions apply:
(a) “Animal” means a domestic animal and includes an animal that is wild by nature
but has been domesticated;
(b) “Burnable Debris” means those materials permitted to be burned in a designated
firepit and in accordance with statutes and bylaws written to protect and enhance
the environment;
(c) “Camping Accommodation Unit” means:
i. A tent;
ii. A tent trailer;
iii. A camper trailer;
iv. A fifth wheel;
v. A motorhome;
vi. A van or truck camper;
vii. A converted bus; or
Page 1 of 13
BYLAW NO. 1864
viii. Other motorized accommodation unit;
used by a person as shelter equipment while camping;
(d) “Campsite Rental Agreement” means the agreement issued by a campsite
reservation service or Park Attendant providing payment confirmation and
permission to occupy a designated area of the park including but not limited to
individual campsites, group campsites, multi-unit campsites, and group use areas;
(e) “Chief Administrative Officer” means the Chief Administrative Officer for the
Municipal District of Bonnyville No. 87 appointed by Council, or authorized
delegate;
(f) “Council” means the duly elected Council of the Municipal District of Bonnyville
No. 87;
(g) “Highway” means a highway as defined in the Traffic Safety Act, R.S.A. 2000 c. T-
6, as amended and regulations thereto;
(h) “Individual Campsite” means a campsite in a park or campground designated as
an individual campsite under this Bylaw;
(i) “Motor Vehicle” means a motor vehcile as defined in the Traffic Safety Act, R.S.A.
2000 c. T-6, as amended and regulations thereto;
(j) “Noise” means any sound that, in the judgment of a Peace Officer taking into
account all relevant factors such as the time of day and the type of noise-producing
activity, is deemed to be bothersome or disruptive to individuals or poses a risk to
the well-being, tranquility and safety of individuals within the municipality's limits;
(k) “Off-Highway Vehicle” means an Off-Highway Vehicle as defined in the Traffic
Safety Act, R.S.A. 2000 c. T-6, as amended thereto;
(l) “Park Attendant” means a person appointed as a Park Attendant by the Municipal
District of Bonnyville;
(m) “Park Land” means every recreational area owned or controlled by the Municipal
District of Bonnyville that lies within the limits of the municipality whether such park
land is improved in whole or in part, or remains in its natural state but shall include
other neighbourhood beautification areas, campgrounds, and publicly maintained
areas administered by the municipality;
(n) “Peace Officer” means:
i. Any member of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police;
ii. Any Municipal District of Bonnyville Community Peace Officer; and
iii. The Chief Administrative Officer of the Municipal District of Bonnyville or
any person designated by the Chief Administrative Officer to enter and
inspect property in accordance with the provisions of this Bylaw;
Page 2 of 13
BYLAW NO. 1864
(o) “Primary Campsite Renter” means the individual named on the Site Rental
Agreement;
(p) “Prohibited Item” means an item that could be deemed as threatening:, including
but not limited to a rifle, shotgun, pistol, handgun, target pistol, air rifle, pellet gun,
hunting bow, crossbow, slingshot, fireworks, and paintball gun;
(q) “Unsatisfactory Condition” means a condition of unreasonable accumulation of
materials, debris and/or refuse within parkland in the opinion of a Peace Officer
having regard for all circumstances;
(r) “Violation Ticket” means a ticket or similar document issued by the Municipal
District of Bonnyville No. 87 pursuant to Part II of the Provincial Offences
Procedures Act, R.S.A. 2000, C. P-34.
2 RULES
2.1 GENERAL
(a) Campgrounds will be closed between October 1st and April 30th unless otherwise
approved by the Chief Administrative Officer or delegate.
(b) A person who enters a park shall comply with:
i. Any lawful orders and instructions made or issued pursuant to this
Bylaw, and
ii. Instructions, prohibitions and directions prescribed by all lawfully
designated and erected signs and notices.
(c) A person registering to be the Primary Campsite Renter for a campsite must be a
minimum of 18 years of age at the time of registration and may be required to
present photograph identification at any time for confirmation.
(d) The collection and use of personal information from the Primary Campsite Renter
shall be in accordance with the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy
(FOIP) Act, R.S.A. 2000, c. F-25.
(e) All persons renting a campsite shall register with the Park Attendant upon arrival
where a sign or notice is located at or near the entrance to the park.
(f) If a park’s campsite occupant violates this Bylaw and their name and contact
information cannot be obtained, the registered Primary Campsite Renter for the
campsite may be held responsible for any applicable offences.
(g) A person vacating a campsite must restore it to a clean condition; if vacated and
left in an unsatisfactory condition, the Primary Campsite Renter may be issued a
penalty under this Bylaw.
(h) Pursuant to Section 3.1 (g), the vacated campsite must be inspected by the
Municipal District of Bonnyville No. 87 within four (4) hours of vacancy for the
Page 3 of 13
BYLAW NO. 1864
previous Primary Campsite Renter to be held liable.
(i) A person using a park shall keep the land and improvements in a condition
satisfactory to the Chief Administrative Officer or delegate.
(j) A person may consume liquor or cannabis within park lands within registered
campsites only and in accordance with the Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis
Act, R.S.A. 2000, c. G-1.
(k) Open liquor and cannabis shall be prohibited in public areas including but not
limited to:
i. On highways, trails and walking paths;
ii. On public beaches;
iii. In washrooms, outhouses and shower buildings; and
iv. In picnic shelters.
(l) No person shall interfere with the rights of others to the quiet and peaceful
enjoyment of a park.
(m) Any individual who has been evicted from a park under this Bylaw shall be banned
from entering or trying to enter any municipal operated park for a period of one (1)
year.
(n) No person shall enter or remain in any park or portion of a park where travel or
access restrictions have been imposed by the Municipal District of Bonnyville No.
87.
(o) No person shall display or post any signs or advertisements in the park other than
those approved by the Chief Administrative Officer or delegate.
(p) No person shall remove, deface, damage, or destroy any property, object,
equipment, facility or grounds in any park, whether created by natural means or
otherwise.
(q) No person shall hunt or discharge a firearm or use a prohibited item within a park.
(r) No person shall conduct business operations in a park unless they have received
written approval from the Chief Administrative Officer or delegate.
2.2 WASTE DISPOSAL
(a) No person shall deposit liquid or solid waste in a park except in a receptacle or
area provided for that purpose by the Municipal District of Bonnyville No. 87.
(b) No person shall bring commercial or residential waste matter into a park for
disposal.
(c) Individuals shall be accountable for disposing of waste, regardless of the
Page 4 of 13
BYLAW NO. 1864
availability of a nearby disposal reciprocal.
(d) No person shall bathe or clean clothing, fish, cooking or eating utensils, vehicles
or other equipment at or near a well, spigot or pump in any park.
(e) No person shall remove water from a park, except by a Primary Campsite Renter
for the personal use of themselves and their party in their camping accommodation
unit for the duration of the registration.
2.3 CAMPSITE RENTAL AGREEMENTS
(a) Campsite Rental Agreements will be issued through the online reservation system
or the Municipal District of Bonnyville No. 87.
(b) Campsite rental reservations and agreements shall be issued on a first-come, first-
served basis.
(c) No person shall camp overnight in a park except in an area designated for that
purpose unless they have received written permission from the Chief
Administrative Officer or delegate.
2.4 CAMPSITE OCCUPATION
(a) Check in times are as follows:
i. Check in: 2:00 p.m.
ii. Check out: 12:00 p.m., unless otherwise approved by the Chief
Administrative Officer or delegate.
(b) No person shall generate noise between the hours of 11:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m.,
unless otherwise approved in writing by the Chief Administrative Officer or
delegate.
(c) Each campsite that can accommodate more than one camping accommodation
unit shall be subject to an additional unit fee as determined by the campground
rate schedule set by the Municipal District of Bonnyville No. 87.
(d) All vehicles and equipment shall remain within the boundaries of the campsite of
the registered guest, or a designated parking area, and shall not impede traffic at
any time, or into an adjacent campsite or park area.
(e) A basic Campsite Rental Agreement fee covers the following maximum number of
units:
i. One (1) camping accommodation unit and two (2) tents; or
ii. Three (3) tents
(f) No person who is visiting a person camped in an individual campsite, shall park
their vehicle at the campsite that is:
Page 5 of 13
BYLAW NO. 1864
i. in a manner or at a location that impedes traffic, or
ii. in a location prohibited by sign.
(g) The number of occupants permitted in each site shall not exceed eight (8) persons.
(h) No person shall camp for more than 14 consecutive days within the same campsite
without the written permission of the Chief Administrative Officer or delegate, with
the exception of seasonal reservations at approved campgrounds.
(i) For the purpose of Section 2.4(h), the Primary Campsite Renter must wait for at
least 24 hours after checking out of a campsite at the end of a 14-day period before
they can re-register the campsite.
(j) In the event that a Primary Campsite Renter receives notification to vacate a
campsite whether by contravention of this Bylaw, or due to safety concerns, the
Primary Campsite Renter shall vacate the campsite within one (1) hour from
receiving such notice, or as otherwise required under such notice.
(k) On the expiry or cancellation of a Campsite Rental Agreement the Primary
Campsite Renter shall ensure that the campsite is vacated and that all shelter
equipment and other property belongings are removed.
2.5 BURNING
(a) No person shall set, light or maintain a fire in a park except in a fireplace, pit or
other facilities designed for that purpose and is confined to either a non-
combustible container or portable appliance, which is set for the purpose of:
i. cooking food,
ii. obtaining warmth, or
iii. viewing for pleasure.
(b) Such fire may only be fueled with seasoned wood, charcoal, coal, natural gas or
propane.
(c) A person may only use burnable debris for fuel purposes in a campground in
accordance with Section 2.5(a).
(d) Fireworks and the discharge of fireworks are prohibited within the confines of parks
operated by the Municipal District of Bonnyville No. 87.
(e) Should a fire hazard be identified by the Bonnyville Regional Fire Authority, Chief
Administrative Officer or delegate, Peace Officer, or Fire Guardian, fires within the
park will be prohibited and restrictions will be posted.
(f) Strict adherence to fire bans must be followed at all times when in place.
(g) No person shall leave a fire unattended or allow it to spread.
Page 6 of 13
BYLAW NO. 1864
(h) The disposal of hot coals, ashes, embers or any other burning or smoldering
materials shall be allowed only in areas pursuant to Section 2.5(a) or another
disposal reciprocal provided by the Park Attendant.
(i) A person shall extinguish all fires, hot coals, or smoldering materials before leaving
the campsite.
(j) When a fire is deemed to be unsafe by the Chief Administrative Officer or delegate,
or a Park Attendant, the person or Park Attendant shall extinguish the flames.
2.6 VEHICLES
(a) No person shall operate a motor vehicle in a park except on a highway.
(b) A Park Attendant or Peace Officer may prohibit the entry of a vehicle into any part
of any park.
(c) No person shall, within a park, operate or ride an off-highway vehicle except at
approved campgrounds. Persons in violation of this Section may be fined in
accordance with the Municipal District of Bonnyville No. 87 Consolidated Public
Safety Bylaw.
(d) Notwithstanding Section 2.6(c), a Park Attendant or Peace Officer may operate an
off-highway vehicle within a park for the purposes of performing their duties within
the park.
(e) In the allowable areas of the approved campgrounds, pursuant to the Traffic Safety
Act, R.S.A. 2000, c. T-6 or this Bylaw, persons shall operate the off-highway
vehicle as per the manufacturer's recommendations.
(f) Entrances and exits of off-highway vehicles of surrounding trails shall be made
directly and by the shortest route to the owner’s campsite.
(g) No person who is the owner or operator of an off-highway vehicle may operate or
permit any other person to operate the off-highway vehicle when there is not a
subsisting certificate of registration and/or a financial responsibility card indicating
valid insurance issued pursuant to the Traffic Safety Act, R.S.A. 2000, c. T-6.
2.7 ANIMAL CONTROL
(a) A Park Attendant or Peace Officer may refuse to admit to a park or require to be
removed from a park, any animal considered not under control, deemed a
nuisance, or may cause damage to the life, safety, health, property or comfort of
any person in the park.
(b) Individuals responsible for an animal must not bring it into a park or permit its entry
unless the animal is contained in a cage or controlled by a leash, chain, or similar
device that does not exceed 3 meters in length.
(c) Individuals responsible for the custody or control of an animal in a park shall not
allow the animal to enter, or remain in, or on, any area in a park that is:
Page 7 of 13
BYLAW NO. 1864
i. a designated swimming area;
ii. a beach area adjacent to a designated swimming area;
iii. a public washroom, change house, concession, public shelter, or other public
building or structure; or
iv. an area where signs are posted prohibiting animals.
(d) A Peace Officers is authorized to capture and impound in an animal shelter any
animal which is at large including dogs pursuant to the Municipal District of
Bonnyville No. 87 Consolidated Public Safety Bylaw.
(e) It is prohibited to bring or allow horses, ponies, or other pack animals into a park
unless they are in a designated equestrian area or have received written approval
from the Chief Administrative Officer or delegate.
2.8 PARK OPERATIONS
(a) A Park Attendant or Peace Officer may, at any time, enter and inspect any
occupied or unoccupied campsite within a park.
(b) A Park Attendant or Peace Officer may order the repair, alteration, improvement,
or removal of any item(s) deemed to be unsafe in the park.
(c) The Chief Administrative Officer or delegate, or a Peace Officer, may order any
person in a park to stop or refrain from any action, omission or conduct that in the
opinion of the Chief Administrative Officer or delegate, or Peace Officer is
dangerous to life or property or detrimental to the use and enjoyment of the park
by other persons.
(d) A Park Attendant or Peace Officer may, at any time, require a person to declare
their intended use of the park.
(e) The Chief Administrative Officer or delegate, or a Peace Officer may remove or
evict, or cause to be removed or evicted, from the park, any person:
i. failing to comply with any provision of this Bylaw, or
ii. creating a nuisance or disturbance, or trespassing, or any other undesirable
act as defined under this Bylaw or any other municipal bylaw.
(f) If, in the opinion of the Chief Administrative Officer or delegate a nuisance exists,
on any site which is subject to a Campsite Rental Agreement, the Chief
Administrative Officer or delegate, or a Peace Officer may, in writing, order the
person causing the nuisance to abate the nuisance or clean the site, or both.
(g) Where a person or Primary Campsite Renter fails to comply with an order made
pursuant to Section 2.8(f) of this Bylaw, the Chief Administrative Officer or delegate
may take steps necessary to abate the nuisance or clean the site, or both.
i. Any costs incurred pursuant to Section 2.8(g) may be charged back to the
Page 8 of 13
BYLAW NO. 1864
Campsite Rental Agreement holder.
(h) The Chief Administrative Officer or delegate may cancel or suspend a Campsite
Rental Agreement issued in accordance with this Bylaw if the Primary Campsite
Renter or guest(s) for any contraventions of this Bylaw, or any other municipal
bylaw, or any of the terms of conditions of the Campsite Rental Agreement.
3 AUTHORITY OF THE CHIEF ADMINISTRATIVE OFFICER
3.1 The Chief Administrative Officer or delegate may exercise any authority already
expressed in this Bylaw as well as:
(a) Subject to the Municipal District of Bonnyville No. 87 Consolidated Public Safety
Bylaw, control and prohibit the movement of vehicular, pedestrian and other traffic
by means of signs and notices being designated and erected.
(b) Designate and erect other signs and notices governing and prohibiting activities
that are provided for in this Bylaw.
(c) Appoint persons necessary for the administration of this Bylaw as Park Attendants.
(d) Determine if a person shall be prohibited from accessing any park and the duration
of such prohibition .
4 AUTHORITY OF A PEACE OFFICER
4.1 A Peace Officer may seize, remove, and/or dispose of a motor vehicle, off highway
vehicle, aircraft, boat, trailer, equipment, appliance, article or object in accordance with
this Bylaw, if upon inspection it:
(a) remains in an area after the authorization to be in that area has expired;
(b) is located in a prohibited area;
(c) is located in an area where parking is prohibited by sign;
(d) is involved in a contravention of this Bylaw, regardless if it is found in the
possession of the person alleged to have committed the contravention; or
(e) is deemed by the Peace Officer to be abandoned.
4.2 A Peace Officer shall allow the owner of an item seized under Section 4.1 to claim it
after determining that the risk of the offense being repeated has diminished.
4.3 Where a Peace Officer moves or stores an item or causes it to be moved or stored
under this Section, the cost of the doing so:
(a) shall be the responsibility of the owner of the item;
(b) constitutes a lien on the item;
(c) may be recovered from the owner in an action for debt; and
Page 9 of 13
BYLAW NO. 1864
(d) must be paid before the item is released to the owner or person otherwise
authorized to retrieve it.
4.4 Should an item seized under Section 4.1 not be claimed within 60 days, it shall become
the property of the Municipal District of Bonnyville No. 87 for disposal at the Chief
Administrative Officer or delegates discretion, with the exception of items outlined in
accordance with the Traffic Safety Act, R.S.A. 2000, c. T-6.
4.5 A Peace Officer may issue a Violation Ticket for any contravention of this Bylaw in
accordance with Schedule “A” attached to and forming part of this Bylaw and served in
accordance with Section 4.6. The Violation Ticket shall require payment to the
Municipal District of Bonnyville No. 87 for the specified penalty amount for that offence.
4.6 A Violation Ticket or written notice of contravention of this Bylaw shall be deemed to be
sufficiently served if:
(a) Served personally on the accused;
(b) Mailed to the address of the Registered Owner of the Vehicle concerned or the
person concerned;
(c) Mailed to the address provided by the Primary Campsite Renter upon registration
for the campsite;
(d) Mailed to the address provided on Government issued identification; or
(e) Attached or left upon the vehicle in respect of which the offence is alleged to have
been committed.
5 PENALTIES
5.1 Every person who contravenes any provisions of this Bylaw, enumerated in Schedule
“A” herein, is guilty of an offence and shall be held liable on summary conviction to the
penalty specified therein for such offense.
5.2 Where payment of a penalty for a Violation Ticket is received within 15 days from the
date of issue, the voluntary payment shall be reduced by ten ($10.00) dollars.
5.3 Following the fifteenth day from receiving a Violation Ticket, a person may pay the ticket
issued as a late payment and the Municipal District of Bonnyville No. 87 will accept the
penalty payment as outlined in Schedule "A" instead of pursuing prosecution.
6 REPEAL
6.1 Upon third reading of Bylaw No. 1864, Bylaw No. 1624 and all amendments thereto are
hereby repealed.
7 SEVERABILITY
7.1 It is the intention of Council that each separate provision of this Bylaw shall be deemed
independent of all other provisions herein and it is the further intention of Council that if
any provision of this Bylaw is declared invalid by a court of competent jurisdiction, then
Page 10 of 13
BYLAW NO. 1864
the invalid portion shall be severed and the remainder of the Bylaw is deemed valid and
enforceable.
8 EFFECTIVE DATE
8.1 That this Bylaw shall come into force and have effect from and after the date of third
and final reading thereof.
READ A FIRST TIME IN COUNCIL THIS 9th DAY OF APRIL, 2024.
READ A SECOND TIME, AS AMENDED, IN COUNCIL
THIS 23RD DAY OF APRIL, 2024.

M.D. Operated
The Municipal District of Bonnyville owns and operates 12 campgrounds and parks within its municipal boundary. All are well maintained and offer unique camping experiences geared towards the park’s natural advantages.
Please note - all M.D. Campgrounds now offer online reservations. Visit letscamp.ca to book online.
Campground rates, contact numbers, and reservation website addresses may be subject to change.
Provincially / Privately Operated
Be sure to check out the the parks and campgrounds that are provincial and privately operated as well.
Seasonal Campgrounds
If you’re looking for a place to set up camp all summer long, we have a few places in our area where you can do that. Click here for a list of all of the seasonal campgrounds in our area .

Floatingstone
Floatingstone Lake Campground
Located 4 km west & 8 km north of Ashmont in a naturally wooded area abutting the south shore.
The park is maintained and groomed in the most meticulous fashion to ensure its natural beauty.
"Our Go-To Spot"
This campground is always wonderfully maintained. The staff are probably the friendliest we have ever encountered. After our 5th trip, we are even more convinced that we will be back many more times. The beach is meticulously maintained, the outhouses are clean and located in great spots, and the added amenities make this easy enough to work from home at the campground.
-2024 review
"Best camping spot"
We absolutely love it there and would recommend and to everyone. Bernadette and Tim are incredible and do an amazing job attending to the campers and campground. Been going there for several years now and since they started caring for the property it has been even better.
-2024 review
"Heavenly place to camp"
This is the most wonderful campground. The beach is sandy and clean, the water is clean and perfect depth for the kids to play safely. The caretakers treated my three sons and I like their family and they were so very helpful and kind. I really loved my time camping here. It’s like heaven.
The trails are fun to adventure on and all are connected so no worries of getting lost.
The bathrooms and showers are clean and well-kept. There are lots of things to keep the kids busy; playgrounds and on the beach volleyball, swimming and digging in the sand. There's also a nice little floating wharf to fish off. This place has everything you need to have a perfect fun and relaxing camping trip. Don’t miss out on this gem of a place.
-2024 review
"Favourite Campground"
This is our second time staying at this campground and we love it. A little over two hours away from Edmonton and worth the drive. The sites are a good size, staff are very friendly and the beach is amazing. There are flush toilets & showers if you want, as well as outhouses available. Highly recommend.
-2024 review
Book through Let's Camp
Blue-green Algae Advisory
Issued July 14, 2026
Visitors to Floatingstone are advised to take the following precautions:
Avoid all contact with cyanobacterial blooms. If contact occurs, wash with tap water as soon as possible.
Do not swim or wade or allow your pets to swim or wade in any areas where cyanobacteria is visible.
Do not feed whole fish or fish trimmings from this lake to your pets.
Consider limiting human consumption of whole fish and fish trimmings from this lake, as it is known that fish may store toxins in their liver. (People can safely consume fish fillets from this lake; however, consumption should be limited as fish may store toxins in their liver).
View more details on the AHS website.

Campground Feature: Westcove Municipal Recreation Area
Located 15 minutes north of St. Paul by Vincent Lake, Westcove is a naturally wooded area; truly a family park with something for everyone. In the winter, take advantage of the Nordic Ski Trail Network developed by the Lakeland Cross Country Ski Club volunteers.
Learn More
Camping Fees and Rental Rates
Our camping rates are All-Season rates.
The County campgrounds do not have designated tenting areas, but tenting can be enjoyed within each campsite at the same rates below.
Reservation Policy
When making a reservation, full payment is required in advance for each day booked. A 48-hour Cancellation Policy is in effect.
An Administration Fee equivalent to a one-night stay per site will remain on your credit card for any cancellations.
Any cancellation made less than 48 hours in advance will not receive a refund .
Campers may book up to 14 consecutive days at Floatingstone, Lac Bellevue, and Stoney Lake.
However, Westcove bookings may be for 4 weeks at a time.

It’s important to sit down with your family and make your own emergency plan so that each family member knows what to do if an emergency occurs.
Should an emergency occur, family members may not be together and could be at school, home or work.

Fire/Burn Permits
County of St. Paul fire permits are issued online. Residents no longer need to visit the County Administration Office or the Town of Elk Point Office for a fire permit.
How to Apply
Open the Permit Form
Access the Fire Permit Application Form through our Laserfiche Portal.
Add Permit Details
With your contact information, you will also need to share the purpose of the burn and the legal land location (part, section, township and range) of the property for the intended burn.
E-Sign and Submit
You will receive an email stating the permit has been received and will be reviewed shortly. Please allow up to 2 business days for review. Approved permits will be sent via email as a PDF attachment and are valid for 14 days from the date of issue.

Best Practice Guidelines for Burning Stubble within the County

Fire Advisory Systems Activities Policy
Help Manage the Risks of Fires
The County of St. Paul recognizes that residents and visitors may want to ignite an open-air fire within County boundaries. As a result, it is necessary to have guidelines for issuing fire restrictions and fire bans to regulate open-air fires.
The County has established a clear guide under the Fire Systems Activities Policy for levels of fire activity restrictions within its borders.
Adhere to the following mitigation tactics:
Landowners who are issued Fire Permits must contact the Bonnyville 911 Dispatch Service prior to igniting their fire at 780-826-7446.
All approved fire permits are subject to Provincial or Local Fire Bans, declared upon the threat of a fire within County boundaries.
Fires must be tended to at all times and completely extinguished before left unattended. Residents with burn barrels must have a spark-arresting screen in place.
Any brush piles that were ignited over the winter should be checked to ensure that they are completely extinguished, that there is no danger of relighting or ground fire starting.
During Fire Bans, we strongly discourage ATV/UTV recreational use until conditions improve. If ATV use is necessary, be prepared/equipped to put out fires that result from sparks given off by the ATV.
FireSmart - Wildfire Safety
Wildfire season is from March 1-October 31 each year. In some of those days, when snow is on the ground, wildfires are probably the last thing on your mind. But these are crucial points to help reduce the threat of wildfire for warmer, drier months.
The Province partnered with FireSmart, a framework for prevention and mitigation measures to reduce wildfire threat, to educate residents on how to protect your home and property. Download the FireSmart App and check out the FireSmart resources to prepare and protect your home.

The County of St. Paul is supported by the Bonnyville Regional Fire Authority who is proud to offer members of the Deaf, Deafened, Hard of Hearing and Speech Impaired (DHHSI) Community for a new 'text with 9-1-1' service for easier communication with emergency services.
Contact your cell and/or wireless provider to ensure that your phone will support T9-1-1. Register with your provider(s) to enable this service. This service is only available to the DHHSI community and is only to be used in emergency situations.
To use this service, continue to call 9-1-1 with your enabled device. The operator will receive a notification if the caller's device has been registered for T9-1-1. If no answer to the operator's voice is received, the operator will then begin sending text messages to the registered phone.
