Frequently Asked Questions
Is there a cost for putting out a fire on a resident’s property?
Expand
A minimum fee and/or costs incurred by the County or Fire Departments may be charged to the landowner if the Fire Department or County is called upon to respond or extinguish a fire. Additional charges may be pending under the Forest and Prairie Protection Act and/or County Fee Schedule Bylaw.
See the County of St. Paul Fee Schedule for information.
Will I be charged for fires that start in ditches or in a right-of-way that spreads to my property?
Expand
Usually there is no cost as we cannot show how a fire in the ditch was started.
Do I need a burn permit?
Expand
Fire permits are required on a year-round basis for all types of open burning.
Open burning includes the burning of brush piles or garbage in barrels, open pits, etc. – where smoke is released into the open air.
What is the cost for a burn permit?
Expand
There is no fee for a burn permit.
How do I get a fire/burn permit?
Expand
Applications for a fire permit can be made online .
How long is a fire permit valid?
Expand
Fire permits are valid for 14 days from the issue date. Plan accordingly, as permits may take up to two business days for approval.
Can I burn anything during a Fire Ban?
Expand
A fire ban suspends or cancels any Fire Permits. Also not allowed are
- wood campfires on private land and provincial campgrounds
- backyard firepits
- barbeques using charcoal briquettes
- fireworks
What is allowed during a Fire Ban
- Portable propane fire pits contained within designated fire pits and gas or propane stoves and barbeques designed for cooking or heating
What's the difference between a Fire Restriction and a Fire Ban?
Expand
For a fire restriction and fire ban, while all burn permits are cancelled and no new ones are issued, wood campfires are still permitted in a fire restriction. Our Fire Advisory System Policy provides more details.
How do I become a volunteer firefighter?
Expand
Contact the Fire Chief for your area at the Ashmont, Mallaig, Elk Point or St. Paul Fire Departments.
How do I contact the Bylaw Enforcement Officer?
Expand
At this time, please direct all bylaw inquiries to:
CAO, Jason Wallsmith: 780-646-6742
Director of Community Services, Jason Storch: 780-646-6768
Are fireworks allowed in the County?
Expand
Fireworks are allowed within the County. However, under Bylaw 2021-12 Fire Protection Services, no person shall discharge fireworks on any County-owned or managed lands without prior approval from Council.
Written permission of a Forest Officer is required during a Fire Advisory and Fire Restriction.
Fireworks are not allowed during a Fire Ban.
How do I contact RCMP directly?
Expand
For non-emergencies (e.g. follow-up on existing file, to speak to a specific member, general inquiries), contact:
St. Paul RCMP Office: 780-645-8870
Saddle Lake RCMP Office: 780-726-3201
Elk Point RCMP Office: 780-724-3964.
For emergencies, call 9-1-1.

We are proud to offer a number of facilities and services for a higher quality of life.

Airports
St. Paul Airport
The St. Paul Municipal Airport is an all-weather facility located approximately 3 kilometres west of St. Paul on Hwy 29.
The runway is 3,498 feet in length and 100 feet in width.
Fact Sheet & Contact Info
Elk Point Municipal Airport
Elk Point Municipal Airport is an excellent facility located approximately 8 kilometres east of Elk Point on secondary Hwy 646.
The airport has a runway of 4,492 feet in length and a width of 74 feet with a tie-down.
Fact Sheet & Contact Info
Cemeteries
There are 33 cemeteries within the County of St. Paul, with 10 of those owned and administered by the County.
The County of St. Paul provides all-season maintenance and operations to the County of St. Paul-owned cemeteries. We perform turf and roadway maintenance, horticulture services and landscaping restorations. We also create and make beautiful signage at each County of St. Paul-owned cemeteries.
The responsibility for the c
emeteries (as listed) falls within the County Community Services department. The Cemetery Board assumes responsibility concerned with the management, planning, and maintenance of those cemeteries owned by the County.
Burials & Plots
To arrange for a burial, reserve a plot, or for more
information about the County-owned cemeteries, please contact the
County Administration Office
. We do not arrange for funerals or headstones.
Visiting
The cemeteries are open to the public 24 hours each day,
seven days a week.
We provide staff to assist with grave locations between the hours of 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday.

Reservations for 2026 Camping Season
Please stay tuned to this page for updates or letscamp.ca
Stays of one week or more begin March 30, 2026. All other reservations open April 1.
Campground rates and reservation website addresses may be subject to change. All prices are subject to GST and site fees.
Seasonal Camping is now available for Muriel Lake M.D. Park. Set up once, and stay all summer May 1 – September 30).
Monthly cabin rental available at Vezeau Beach M.D. Park. Please call 780-826-2245.
Cancellation Policy
In the event that you have to cancel your reservation, please provide at least 72 hours notice, prior to your expected check-in. One night's stay will be deducted from your camping fees for full or partial cancellations.
Failure to notify the campground park attendant or manage your booking online within 72 hours prior to check-in will result in the loss of your entire camping fee.
Rules and Regulations
No person shall interfere with the rights of others to the quiet and peaceful enjoyment of the park.
If generators are needed, please refrain from running your generators continuously throughout the day.
There will be zero tolerance for excessive noise from 11 p.m. to 7 a.m.
Park guests are expected to maintain clean sites. Please use garbage bins for waste - not fire pits. Campsites left in an unacceptable condition may result in a fine of $200 - $400.
Alcohol is not allowed off of your assigned campsite at any time.
Cannabis is not allowed off of your assigned campsite at any time.
All dogs must be leashed AT ALL TIMES. Dogs are not allowed on the beach AT ANY TIME. Cleaning up after your pets is mandatory.
The swimming and playground areas are NOT supervised. Use at your own risk.
Fireworks are prohibited in all M.D. Parks.
OHVs are prohibited inside the park ( except Pelican Point) .
For further rules and regulations please see
B
ylaw 1812
and
B
ylaw 1864
.
Chickenhill Lake
Chickenhill Lake M.D. Park
This little gem has 29, 30-amp powered sites. Grab a lakefront spot at Chickenhill Lake M.D. Park for great views of the sunset or set up in one of the forested sites to enjoy private, treed sites. If you’re looking for a calm and quiet lake to enjoy an afternoon in your canoe or on your paddleboard, look no further! Remember to bring your volleyball — the beach court here is full of soft sand, perfect for a day of friendly competition!
Rural Address: 59314 RGE RD 482.
How to get here: south of Hwy. 28 (at Glendon intersection) on Hwy. 882 (Rge. Rd. 484) for 6.4 km, east on Twp. Rd. 594 for 3.3 km, and then south on Rge. Rd. 482 for one km. From St. Paul go north on Hwy. 881 and east on Twp. Rd. 594 for 28.9 km.
Online reservations open for bookings of a week or more on March 30 at 8:30 a.m. General reservations open April 1 at 8:30 a.m. Park opens May 8, 2026.
Book online here
Cold Lake
Cold Lake M.D. Park
NEW IN 2026 – Our friendly staff will greet you at the new park office and gate.
From lakefront sites to walk-up tent sites, the Cold Lake M.D. Park offers 145 power and 14 non-powered sites. There is also potable water (including RV fill), flush toilets, coin-operated showers, and laundry on site. Find snacks, cold treats, and ice at our onsite store. Registered guests also have access to the boat launch located on the north end of the campground.
This campground provides a great adventure base camp. Take a short five minute walk to Kinosoo Beach and enjoy amenities such as a concession, multiple ice cream vendors, water sport rentals, basketball and volleyball courts, and the lakeside splash park.
Are you looking for a unique place to hold a celebration or private event? Check out our new picnic shelter, available for half-day or full-day rentals.
Located at: 2301-1 Ave. in Cold Lake.
Online reservations open for bookings of a week or more on March 30 at 8:30 a.m. General reservations open April 1 at 8:30 a.m. Park opens May 8, 2026.
Book online here
French Bay on Cold Lake M.D. Park
Camping at French Bay M.D. Park is like a nostalgic time machine, whisking you back to the good old days of unplugged adventures, while having modern comforts just a hop, skip, and a jump away! French Bay offers 10 non-power sites, a boat launch at the upper sites (use dependent on lake levels), a day use beach area, and swimming at the lower campsite. Non-potable water is available via hand pump.
Looking for adventure? Check out the 60-foot-tall Aerial Adventure Park or Target Golf located minutes away at Kinosoo Ridge Resort.
Rural Address: #2 63218 RGE RD 411.
How to get here: located 15 km northeast of Cold Lake, one km south of Kinosoo Ridge Resort, on the southeast shore of Cold Lake.
Online reservations open for bookings of a week or more on March 30 at 8:30 a.m. General reservations open April 1 at 8:30 a.m. Park opens May 8, 2026.
Book online here
Crane Lake
Crane Lake M.D. Park
Where the lake and forest meet, you’ll find a relaxing atmosphere at Crane Lake M.D. Park East. With 29, 30-amp power sites, hand pump for non-potable water, beach, and playground, this a great getaway for the whole family.
At Crane Lake M.D. Park West, you are never far from the lake! This campground offers 23, 30-amp power sites, a large beach, boat mooring, camp kitchen, and non-potable water. This clear lake is enjoyed by anglers, water sports enthusiasts, and swimmers alike!
East Side Rural Address: 64005 RGE RD 443.
West Side Rural Address: 64002 RGE RD 444.
How to get here: located 25 km west of Cold Lake along
Hwy. 55, five km north on Rge. Rd. 444.
Online reservations open for bookings of a week or more on March 30 at 8:30 a.m. General reservations open April 1 at 8:30 a.m. Park opens May 8, 2026.
Book online here
Ethel Lake
Ethel Lake M.D. Park
With only 11 non-power sites, Ethel Lake M.D. Park may be small, but it has a lot to keep you and your family occupied for a day or a week. Whether you have a pontoon or a kayak, it’s a great lake to spend the day on. After dinner, try your aim at the horseshoe pits.
Rural Address: 64232 RGE RD 431.
How to get here: located eight km west on Hwy. 55 and 10 km north on Hwy. 897.
Online reservations open for bookings of a week or more on March 30 at 8:30 a.m. General reservations open April 1 at 8:30 a.m. Park opens May 8, 2026.
Book online here
Minnie Lake
Minnie Lake M.D. Parks
Minnie Lake M.D. Park East offers an amazing getaway with 11, 30-amp power sites. Everything you need is here including, a day use picnic area, change rooms, beach with swimming area, diving platform, frisbee golf, and volleyball court. Want to rent a paddle board or feeling a little snacky? Come check out the store!
At Minnie Lake M.D. Park West, you’ll find seven large 30-amp power sites — the perfect venue for a family reunion! You’ll also find a boat launch and dock. This picturesque small lake is great for a variety of water activities.
East Side Rural Address: #17 61219 RGE RD 482.
West Side Rural Address: #45 61219 RGE RD 482.
How to get here: located five minutes northeast of Glendon, north off Hwy. 660.
Online reservations open for bookings of a week or more on March 30 at 8:30 a.m. General reservations open April 1 at 8:30 a.m. Park opens May 8, 2026.
Book online here
Moose Lake
Pelican Point on Moose Lake M.D. Park
Bring your quad or side-by-side to the M.D.’s Pelican Point campground for a trip full of exploring and fun! All 61 non-power individual sites are OHV friendly. Coming with a group of friends? Reserve one of our two large group sites. Check out the sand dunes outside of the park or hop on the Iron Horse Trail to explore the region.
Looking for a more tranquil experience? Take a walk through the forest and find a treasure trove of berries!
Remember to bring your fishing rod! Cast a line and hook a variety of fish including pike, walleye, and perch. Be sure to review the Alberta Guide to Sportfishing Regulations before reeling in your next big fish story.
Full regulations about OHV use within the park are posted here
.
Rural Address: 61015 RGE RD 474.
How to get here: located two km north of Bonnyville on Hwy. 41, 16 km west on Hwy. 660 and 6.5 km south on Rge. Rd. 474 OR one km north of Glendon, 10 km east on Hwy. 660 and 6.5 km south.
Online reservations open for bookings of a week or more on March 30 at 8:30 a.m. General reservations open April 1 at 8:30 a.m. Park opens May 8, 2026.
Book online here
Vezeau Beach on Moose Lake M.D. Park
Looking for a summer at the lake? Vezeau Beach M.D. Park has it all! This park offers 23 full-service sites (non-potable water) plus three power-only sites on the south shore of Moose Lake. Enjoy the convenience of having coin-operated laundry facilities and showers within walking distance. Head out for a day on the water using our two-lane boat launch with 15-boat slip dock. Kids can find hours of fun waiting for them at the playground and jumping pillow or by borrowing one of the outdoor games.
Spend an afternoon taking on the 18-hole course at the Bonnyville Golf & Country Club, located across the road. Bring your bike or favourite walking shoes and check out the extensive Moose Lake trail system.
When you check in at the Visitor Information & Interpretive Centre at the Shaw House, treat yourself to some delicious ice cream and a souvenir crafted by our talented local artisans!
No camper or tent? No problem! We have a cabin available for monthly bookings! The rental includes power, non-potable water, and a three-piece washroom. Bring your own bedding and linens. Please call 780-826-2245 to book your cabin adventure!
NEW THIS YEAR – The Shaw House is now a licenced facility. Enjoy a locally brewed beverage on the outdoor patio.
Rural Address: #1 46300 TWP RD 611.
How to get here : located five km west of Bonnyville on Hwy. 28
Online reservations open for bookings of a week or more on March 30 at 8:30 a.m. General reservations open April 1 at 8:30 a.m. Park opens May 1, 2026.
Book online here
Muriel Lake
Muriel Lake M.D. Park
With 54, 30-amp power, 39 non-power, and two non-power group areas, Muriel Lake is one of the M.D.’s largest campgrounds.
Featuring 13 kilometres of hiking and biking trails, baseball diamonds, two playgrounds, volleyball court, onsite store, and day use lookout area, this is the perfect play and stay destination! The campground also offers running non-potable water, barrier-free accessible washrooms, showers, and coin laundry.
Get a summer full of camping by booking one of our 20 seasonal sites. Set up your camper once and your getaway will always be ready for you from May 1 to September 30.
EVENTS - To see all events click here.
2026CLAIR – Use this promo code to receive 10% off your stay at Muriel Lake M.D. Park during the Cold Lake Air Show on July 18 and 19, 2026!
Rural Address: 60304 RGE RD 452.
How to get here : located 12 km east off Hwy. 28 (just before the Town of Bonnyville) on Twp. Rd. 610 and six km south on Rge. Rd. 452 (watch for signs).
Online reservations open for bookings of a week or more on March 30 at 8:30 a.m. General reservations open April 1 at 8:30 a.m. Park opens May 1, 2026.
Book online here
Wolf Lake
Wolf Lake M.D. Park
Wolf Lake M.D. Park has 59 non-power sites tucked away in the boreal forest, offering the best place to unplug, unwind, and relax.
Some of the best walleye fishing in the M.D. is here. Make sure you check the Alberta Guide to Sportfishing Regulations and get your walleye tags at mywildalberta.ca .
Non-potable water is available via hand pump.
DID YOU KNOW – Wolf Lake is a birdwatchers paradise! There are almost 300 species of birds in our region, and a lot of them fly over this lake. We fall in the transition zone between Alberta’s aspen parkland and the northern boreal forest.
Rural Address: 65014 RGE RD 475.
How to get here: located 20 km north of Bonnyville on Hwy. 41, 15 km west on Hwy. 55 and 30 km north on Rge. Rd. 475.
Online reservations open for bookings of a week or more on March 30 at 8:30 a.m. General reservations open April 1 at 8:30 a.m. Park opens May 8, 2026.
Book Online
Reservations are strongly recommended for all campgrounds. Campground rates, site details may be subject to change.

BYLAW NO. 1864
A BYLAW OF THE MUNICIPAL DISTRICT OF BONNYVILLE NO. 87, IN THE
PROVINCE OF ALBERTA TO PROVIDE FOR THE CONTROL AND OPERATION OF
PARKS AND CAMPGROUNDS UNDER THE JURISDICTION OF THE MUNICIPALITY
HEREBY CITED AS THE PARKS AND CAMPGROUND BYLAW.
WHEREAS, under the provisions of the Municipal Government Act, R.S.A 2000, Chapter M-26,
and amendments thereto, a Council’s power to pass a bylaw includes a power to amend or repeal
a bylaw;
AND WHEREAS, the Municipal Government Act, Chapter M-26, R.S.A. 2000 grants authority to
Council to pass bylaws with respect to the safety, health and welfare of people and the protection
of people and property;
AND WHEREAS, Council of the Municipal District of Bonnyville No. 87 has established public
parks and campgrounds;
AND WHEREAS, Council of the Municipal District of Bonnyville No. 87 wishes to establish rules
and regulations for the control and operation of its public parks and campgrounds;
NOW THEREFORE, the Council of the Municipal District of Bonnyville No. 87, duly assembled
in the Province of Alberta, hereby enacts the following:
1 DEFINITIONS
1.1 Words in the singular shall include the plural or vice versa whenever the context so
requires.
1.2 In this Bylaw the following definitions apply:
(a) “Animal” means a domestic animal and includes an animal that is wild by nature
but has been domesticated;
(b) “Burnable Debris” means those materials permitted to be burned in a designated
firepit and in accordance with statutes and bylaws written to protect and enhance
the environment;
(c) “Camping Accommodation Unit” means:
i. A tent;
ii. A tent trailer;
iii. A camper trailer;
iv. A fifth wheel;
v. A motorhome;
vi. A van or truck camper;
vii. A converted bus; or
Page 1 of 13
BYLAW NO. 1864
viii. Other motorized accommodation unit;
used by a person as shelter equipment while camping;
(d) “Campsite Rental Agreement” means the agreement issued by a campsite
reservation service or Park Attendant providing payment confirmation and
permission to occupy a designated area of the park including but not limited to
individual campsites, group campsites, multi-unit campsites, and group use areas;
(e) “Chief Administrative Officer” means the Chief Administrative Officer for the
Municipal District of Bonnyville No. 87 appointed by Council, or authorized
delegate;
(f) “Council” means the duly elected Council of the Municipal District of Bonnyville
No. 87;
(g) “Highway” means a highway as defined in the Traffic Safety Act, R.S.A. 2000 c. T-
6, as amended and regulations thereto;
(h) “Individual Campsite” means a campsite in a park or campground designated as
an individual campsite under this Bylaw;
(i) “Motor Vehicle” means a motor vehcile as defined in the Traffic Safety Act, R.S.A.
2000 c. T-6, as amended and regulations thereto;
(j) “Noise” means any sound that, in the judgment of a Peace Officer taking into
account all relevant factors such as the time of day and the type of noise-producing
activity, is deemed to be bothersome or disruptive to individuals or poses a risk to
the well-being, tranquility and safety of individuals within the municipality's limits;
(k) “Off-Highway Vehicle” means an Off-Highway Vehicle as defined in the Traffic
Safety Act, R.S.A. 2000 c. T-6, as amended thereto;
(l) “Park Attendant” means a person appointed as a Park Attendant by the Municipal
District of Bonnyville;
(m) “Park Land” means every recreational area owned or controlled by the Municipal
District of Bonnyville that lies within the limits of the municipality whether such park
land is improved in whole or in part, or remains in its natural state but shall include
other neighbourhood beautification areas, campgrounds, and publicly maintained
areas administered by the municipality;
(n) “Peace Officer” means:
i. Any member of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police;
ii. Any Municipal District of Bonnyville Community Peace Officer; and
iii. The Chief Administrative Officer of the Municipal District of Bonnyville or
any person designated by the Chief Administrative Officer to enter and
inspect property in accordance with the provisions of this Bylaw;
Page 2 of 13
BYLAW NO. 1864
(o) “Primary Campsite Renter” means the individual named on the Site Rental
Agreement;
(p) “Prohibited Item” means an item that could be deemed as threatening:, including
but not limited to a rifle, shotgun, pistol, handgun, target pistol, air rifle, pellet gun,
hunting bow, crossbow, slingshot, fireworks, and paintball gun;
(q) “Unsatisfactory Condition” means a condition of unreasonable accumulation of
materials, debris and/or refuse within parkland in the opinion of a Peace Officer
having regard for all circumstances;
(r) “Violation Ticket” means a ticket or similar document issued by the Municipal
District of Bonnyville No. 87 pursuant to Part II of the Provincial Offences
Procedures Act, R.S.A. 2000, C. P-34.
2 RULES
2.1 GENERAL
(a) Campgrounds will be closed between October 1st and April 30th unless otherwise
approved by the Chief Administrative Officer or delegate.
(b) A person who enters a park shall comply with:
i. Any lawful orders and instructions made or issued pursuant to this
Bylaw, and
ii. Instructions, prohibitions and directions prescribed by all lawfully
designated and erected signs and notices.
(c) A person registering to be the Primary Campsite Renter for a campsite must be a
minimum of 18 years of age at the time of registration and may be required to
present photograph identification at any time for confirmation.
(d) The collection and use of personal information from the Primary Campsite Renter
shall be in accordance with the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy
(FOIP) Act, R.S.A. 2000, c. F-25.
(e) All persons renting a campsite shall register with the Park Attendant upon arrival
where a sign or notice is located at or near the entrance to the park.
(f) If a park’s campsite occupant violates this Bylaw and their name and contact
information cannot be obtained, the registered Primary Campsite Renter for the
campsite may be held responsible for any applicable offences.
(g) A person vacating a campsite must restore it to a clean condition; if vacated and
left in an unsatisfactory condition, the Primary Campsite Renter may be issued a
penalty under this Bylaw.
(h) Pursuant to Section 3.1 (g), the vacated campsite must be inspected by the
Municipal District of Bonnyville No. 87 within four (4) hours of vacancy for the
Page 3 of 13
BYLAW NO. 1864
previous Primary Campsite Renter to be held liable.
(i) A person using a park shall keep the land and improvements in a condition
satisfactory to the Chief Administrative Officer or delegate.
(j) A person may consume liquor or cannabis within park lands within registered
campsites only and in accordance with the Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis
Act, R.S.A. 2000, c. G-1.
(k) Open liquor and cannabis shall be prohibited in public areas including but not
limited to:
i. On highways, trails and walking paths;
ii. On public beaches;
iii. In washrooms, outhouses and shower buildings; and
iv. In picnic shelters.
(l) No person shall interfere with the rights of others to the quiet and peaceful
enjoyment of a park.
(m) Any individual who has been evicted from a park under this Bylaw shall be banned
from entering or trying to enter any municipal operated park for a period of one (1)
year.
(n) No person shall enter or remain in any park or portion of a park where travel or
access restrictions have been imposed by the Municipal District of Bonnyville No.
87.
(o) No person shall display or post any signs or advertisements in the park other than
those approved by the Chief Administrative Officer or delegate.
(p) No person shall remove, deface, damage, or destroy any property, object,
equipment, facility or grounds in any park, whether created by natural means or
otherwise.
(q) No person shall hunt or discharge a firearm or use a prohibited item within a park.
(r) No person shall conduct business operations in a park unless they have received
written approval from the Chief Administrative Officer or delegate.
2.2 WASTE DISPOSAL
(a) No person shall deposit liquid or solid waste in a park except in a receptacle or
area provided for that purpose by the Municipal District of Bonnyville No. 87.
(b) No person shall bring commercial or residential waste matter into a park for
disposal.
(c) Individuals shall be accountable for disposing of waste, regardless of the
Page 4 of 13
BYLAW NO. 1864
availability of a nearby disposal reciprocal.
(d) No person shall bathe or clean clothing, fish, cooking or eating utensils, vehicles
or other equipment at or near a well, spigot or pump in any park.
(e) No person shall remove water from a park, except by a Primary Campsite Renter
for the personal use of themselves and their party in their camping accommodation
unit for the duration of the registration.
2.3 CAMPSITE RENTAL AGREEMENTS
(a) Campsite Rental Agreements will be issued through the online reservation system
or the Municipal District of Bonnyville No. 87.
(b) Campsite rental reservations and agreements shall be issued on a first-come, first-
served basis.
(c) No person shall camp overnight in a park except in an area designated for that
purpose unless they have received written permission from the Chief
Administrative Officer or delegate.
2.4 CAMPSITE OCCUPATION
(a) Check in times are as follows:
i. Check in: 2:00 p.m.
ii. Check out: 12:00 p.m., unless otherwise approved by the Chief
Administrative Officer or delegate.
(b) No person shall generate noise between the hours of 11:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m.,
unless otherwise approved in writing by the Chief Administrative Officer or
delegate.
(c) Each campsite that can accommodate more than one camping accommodation
unit shall be subject to an additional unit fee as determined by the campground
rate schedule set by the Municipal District of Bonnyville No. 87.
(d) All vehicles and equipment shall remain within the boundaries of the campsite of
the registered guest, or a designated parking area, and shall not impede traffic at
any time, or into an adjacent campsite or park area.
(e) A basic Campsite Rental Agreement fee covers the following maximum number of
units:
i. One (1) camping accommodation unit and two (2) tents; or
ii. Three (3) tents
(f) No person who is visiting a person camped in an individual campsite, shall park
their vehicle at the campsite that is:
Page 5 of 13
BYLAW NO. 1864
i. in a manner or at a location that impedes traffic, or
ii. in a location prohibited by sign.
(g) The number of occupants permitted in each site shall not exceed eight (8) persons.
(h) No person shall camp for more than 14 consecutive days within the same campsite
without the written permission of the Chief Administrative Officer or delegate, with
the exception of seasonal reservations at approved campgrounds.
(i) For the purpose of Section 2.4(h), the Primary Campsite Renter must wait for at
least 24 hours after checking out of a campsite at the end of a 14-day period before
they can re-register the campsite.
(j) In the event that a Primary Campsite Renter receives notification to vacate a
campsite whether by contravention of this Bylaw, or due to safety concerns, the
Primary Campsite Renter shall vacate the campsite within one (1) hour from
receiving such notice, or as otherwise required under such notice.
(k) On the expiry or cancellation of a Campsite Rental Agreement the Primary
Campsite Renter shall ensure that the campsite is vacated and that all shelter
equipment and other property belongings are removed.
2.5 BURNING
(a) No person shall set, light or maintain a fire in a park except in a fireplace, pit or
other facilities designed for that purpose and is confined to either a non-
combustible container or portable appliance, which is set for the purpose of:
i. cooking food,
ii. obtaining warmth, or
iii. viewing for pleasure.
(b) Such fire may only be fueled with seasoned wood, charcoal, coal, natural gas or
propane.
(c) A person may only use burnable debris for fuel purposes in a campground in
accordance with Section 2.5(a).
(d) Fireworks and the discharge of fireworks are prohibited within the confines of parks
operated by the Municipal District of Bonnyville No. 87.
(e) Should a fire hazard be identified by the Bonnyville Regional Fire Authority, Chief
Administrative Officer or delegate, Peace Officer, or Fire Guardian, fires within the
park will be prohibited and restrictions will be posted.
(f) Strict adherence to fire bans must be followed at all times when in place.
(g) No person shall leave a fire unattended or allow it to spread.
Page 6 of 13
BYLAW NO. 1864
(h) The disposal of hot coals, ashes, embers or any other burning or smoldering
materials shall be allowed only in areas pursuant to Section 2.5(a) or another
disposal reciprocal provided by the Park Attendant.
(i) A person shall extinguish all fires, hot coals, or smoldering materials before leaving
the campsite.
(j) When a fire is deemed to be unsafe by the Chief Administrative Officer or delegate,
or a Park Attendant, the person or Park Attendant shall extinguish the flames.
2.6 VEHICLES
(a) No person shall operate a motor vehicle in a park except on a highway.
(b) A Park Attendant or Peace Officer may prohibit the entry of a vehicle into any part
of any park.
(c) No person shall, within a park, operate or ride an off-highway vehicle except at
approved campgrounds. Persons in violation of this Section may be fined in
accordance with the Municipal District of Bonnyville No. 87 Consolidated Public
Safety Bylaw.
(d) Notwithstanding Section 2.6(c), a Park Attendant or Peace Officer may operate an
off-highway vehicle within a park for the purposes of performing their duties within
the park.
(e) In the allowable areas of the approved campgrounds, pursuant to the Traffic Safety
Act, R.S.A. 2000, c. T-6 or this Bylaw, persons shall operate the off-highway
vehicle as per the manufacturer's recommendations.
(f) Entrances and exits of off-highway vehicles of surrounding trails shall be made
directly and by the shortest route to the owner’s campsite.
(g) No person who is the owner or operator of an off-highway vehicle may operate or
permit any other person to operate the off-highway vehicle when there is not a
subsisting certificate of registration and/or a financial responsibility card indicating
valid insurance issued pursuant to the Traffic Safety Act, R.S.A. 2000, c. T-6.
2.7 ANIMAL CONTROL
(a) A Park Attendant or Peace Officer may refuse to admit to a park or require to be
removed from a park, any animal considered not under control, deemed a
nuisance, or may cause damage to the life, safety, health, property or comfort of
any person in the park.
(b) Individuals responsible for an animal must not bring it into a park or permit its entry
unless the animal is contained in a cage or controlled by a leash, chain, or similar
device that does not exceed 3 meters in length.
(c) Individuals responsible for the custody or control of an animal in a park shall not
allow the animal to enter, or remain in, or on, any area in a park that is:
Page 7 of 13
BYLAW NO. 1864
i. a designated swimming area;
ii. a beach area adjacent to a designated swimming area;
iii. a public washroom, change house, concession, public shelter, or other public
building or structure; or
iv. an area where signs are posted prohibiting animals.
(d) A Peace Officers is authorized to capture and impound in an animal shelter any
animal which is at large including dogs pursuant to the Municipal District of
Bonnyville No. 87 Consolidated Public Safety Bylaw.
(e) It is prohibited to bring or allow horses, ponies, or other pack animals into a park
unless they are in a designated equestrian area or have received written approval
from the Chief Administrative Officer or delegate.
2.8 PARK OPERATIONS
(a) A Park Attendant or Peace Officer may, at any time, enter and inspect any
occupied or unoccupied campsite within a park.
(b) A Park Attendant or Peace Officer may order the repair, alteration, improvement,
or removal of any item(s) deemed to be unsafe in the park.
(c) The Chief Administrative Officer or delegate, or a Peace Officer, may order any
person in a park to stop or refrain from any action, omission or conduct that in the
opinion of the Chief Administrative Officer or delegate, or Peace Officer is
dangerous to life or property or detrimental to the use and enjoyment of the park
by other persons.
(d) A Park Attendant or Peace Officer may, at any time, require a person to declare
their intended use of the park.
(e) The Chief Administrative Officer or delegate, or a Peace Officer may remove or
evict, or cause to be removed or evicted, from the park, any person:
i. failing to comply with any provision of this Bylaw, or
ii. creating a nuisance or disturbance, or trespassing, or any other undesirable
act as defined under this Bylaw or any other municipal bylaw.
(f) If, in the opinion of the Chief Administrative Officer or delegate a nuisance exists,
on any site which is subject to a Campsite Rental Agreement, the Chief
Administrative Officer or delegate, or a Peace Officer may, in writing, order the
person causing the nuisance to abate the nuisance or clean the site, or both.
(g) Where a person or Primary Campsite Renter fails to comply with an order made
pursuant to Section 2.8(f) of this Bylaw, the Chief Administrative Officer or delegate
may take steps necessary to abate the nuisance or clean the site, or both.
i. Any costs incurred pursuant to Section 2.8(g) may be charged back to the
Page 8 of 13
BYLAW NO. 1864
Campsite Rental Agreement holder.
(h) The Chief Administrative Officer or delegate may cancel or suspend a Campsite
Rental Agreement issued in accordance with this Bylaw if the Primary Campsite
Renter or guest(s) for any contraventions of this Bylaw, or any other municipal
bylaw, or any of the terms of conditions of the Campsite Rental Agreement.
3 AUTHORITY OF THE CHIEF ADMINISTRATIVE OFFICER
3.1 The Chief Administrative Officer or delegate may exercise any authority already
expressed in this Bylaw as well as:
(a) Subject to the Municipal District of Bonnyville No. 87 Consolidated Public Safety
Bylaw, control and prohibit the movement of vehicular, pedestrian and other traffic
by means of signs and notices being designated and erected.
(b) Designate and erect other signs and notices governing and prohibiting activities
that are provided for in this Bylaw.
(c) Appoint persons necessary for the administration of this Bylaw as Park Attendants.
(d) Determine if a person shall be prohibited from accessing any park and the duration
of such prohibition .
4 AUTHORITY OF A PEACE OFFICER
4.1 A Peace Officer may seize, remove, and/or dispose of a motor vehicle, off highway
vehicle, aircraft, boat, trailer, equipment, appliance, article or object in accordance with
this Bylaw, if upon inspection it:
(a) remains in an area after the authorization to be in that area has expired;
(b) is located in a prohibited area;
(c) is located in an area where parking is prohibited by sign;
(d) is involved in a contravention of this Bylaw, regardless if it is found in the
possession of the person alleged to have committed the contravention; or
(e) is deemed by the Peace Officer to be abandoned.
4.2 A Peace Officer shall allow the owner of an item seized under Section 4.1 to claim it
after determining that the risk of the offense being repeated has diminished.
4.3 Where a Peace Officer moves or stores an item or causes it to be moved or stored
under this Section, the cost of the doing so:
(a) shall be the responsibility of the owner of the item;
(b) constitutes a lien on the item;
(c) may be recovered from the owner in an action for debt; and
Page 9 of 13
BYLAW NO. 1864
(d) must be paid before the item is released to the owner or person otherwise
authorized to retrieve it.
4.4 Should an item seized under Section 4.1 not be claimed within 60 days, it shall become
the property of the Municipal District of Bonnyville No. 87 for disposal at the Chief
Administrative Officer or delegates discretion, with the exception of items outlined in
accordance with the Traffic Safety Act, R.S.A. 2000, c. T-6.
4.5 A Peace Officer may issue a Violation Ticket for any contravention of this Bylaw in
accordance with Schedule “A” attached to and forming part of this Bylaw and served in
accordance with Section 4.6. The Violation Ticket shall require payment to the
Municipal District of Bonnyville No. 87 for the specified penalty amount for that offence.
4.6 A Violation Ticket or written notice of contravention of this Bylaw shall be deemed to be
sufficiently served if:
(a) Served personally on the accused;
(b) Mailed to the address of the Registered Owner of the Vehicle concerned or the
person concerned;
(c) Mailed to the address provided by the Primary Campsite Renter upon registration
for the campsite;
(d) Mailed to the address provided on Government issued identification; or
(e) Attached or left upon the vehicle in respect of which the offence is alleged to have
been committed.
5 PENALTIES
5.1 Every person who contravenes any provisions of this Bylaw, enumerated in Schedule
“A” herein, is guilty of an offence and shall be held liable on summary conviction to the
penalty specified therein for such offense.
5.2 Where payment of a penalty for a Violation Ticket is received within 15 days from the
date of issue, the voluntary payment shall be reduced by ten ($10.00) dollars.
5.3 Following the fifteenth day from receiving a Violation Ticket, a person may pay the ticket
issued as a late payment and the Municipal District of Bonnyville No. 87 will accept the
penalty payment as outlined in Schedule "A" instead of pursuing prosecution.
6 REPEAL
6.1 Upon third reading of Bylaw No. 1864, Bylaw No. 1624 and all amendments thereto are
hereby repealed.
7 SEVERABILITY
7.1 It is the intention of Council that each separate provision of this Bylaw shall be deemed
independent of all other provisions herein and it is the further intention of Council that if
any provision of this Bylaw is declared invalid by a court of competent jurisdiction, then
Page 10 of 13
BYLAW NO. 1864
the invalid portion shall be severed and the remainder of the Bylaw is deemed valid and
enforceable.
8 EFFECTIVE DATE
8.1 That this Bylaw shall come into force and have effect from and after the date of third
and final reading thereof.
READ A FIRST TIME IN COUNCIL THIS 9th DAY OF APRIL, 2024.
READ A SECOND TIME, AS AMENDED, IN COUNCIL
THIS 23RD DAY OF APRIL, 2024.

M.D. Operated
The Municipal District of Bonnyville owns and operates 12 campgrounds and parks within its municipal boundary. All are well maintained and offer unique camping experiences geared towards the park’s natural advantages.
Please note - all M.D. Campgrounds now offer online reservations. Visit letscamp.ca to book online.
Campground rates, contact numbers, and reservation website addresses may be subject to change.

Be sure to check out the the parks and campgrounds that are provincial and privately operated as well.

Chepi Sepe Park
The Chepi Sepe Municipal Campground is located along Highway 49 at the East entrance into town. There are 15 full service campsites & 5 pull through stalls with electricity only, a cooking house, showers, information booth, water fill station and a sanitation dump all located in a beautiful park-like setting. During the season, you can book and make payments at: Let’s Camp Chepi Sepe!
The Tourist Information Booth at the campground will have more information on Moonshine Lake Provincial Park, Dunvegan Provincial Park, and other campgrounds in the area.

Parks and Playgrounds

Parks and Playgrounds
Carlyle Lions Park & Campground:
Quiet, well-treed campground situated west of the baseball diamonds. Modern washroom with showers and flush toilets. Dumping station. Golf courses nearby. Heated swimming pool, hot tub, children’s pool and playground all within walking distance. Pet restrictions apply, no large pets allowed in campground, only one pet per site.
Campsites available: May to October, to book call (306) 575-6600
For ball diamond schedule please see link here Carlyle Ball Diamond Schedule
Centennial Park
Centennial Park offers a lovely spot to stop for a break while strolling through at one of it’s park benches, or pack a picnic to have in the gazebo which has two picnic tables. There are many flower bed areas, purple martin houses as well as a newly installed rubber walking path through the park.
West Park
West park is located on the west edge of town and is accessed off of 8th Street west.
Carlyle Communi
ty Playground
Carlyle hosts an inviting playground geared for children ages 0 – 12. It hosts modern play structures that encourage the creative minds of children. Swing sets are available and include three infant swing seats, a four person teeter-totter, a tire swing, park benches, picnic tables and much more. A definite destination for any person(s) who have children!

Strategic Plan
Town of
Carlyle Strategic Plan
Town Council participated in a closed strategic planning session on
March 4, 2021 led by HMC Management Inc., during this session Council created a
vision and mission statement and established priorities for their four-year
term. The Strategic Plan Report and the Operations Plan Report were
reviewed and adopted by council at their April 7, 2021 Regular Meeting.
Town of Carlyle Vision 2025
" Carlyle
is an inclusive and welcoming community which provides a dynamic and
sustainable living environment for families and businesses to thrive.”
Town of Carlyle Mission Statement 2021
"As leaders, the purpose of the Council of the Town of Carlyle is
to create and manage sustainable programs and services for the betterment of
our community.”
T
own of Carlyle Values
Financial Accountability
We are dedicated to being a good
steward of public funds and resources and will strive to attain value for
public funds and, where reasonable, will provide services on a user pay basis.
Healthy Lifestyles/Quality of
Life
In supporting and promoting the
importance of healthy living, we are dedicated to providing healthy
recreational and cultural opportunities for the residents and visitors.
Safe Community/Safe Operations
We are
dedicated to a safe community that provides an environment where people feel
safe, secure, and 'at home’ and will strive for zero harm for our
employees through appropriate training and risk management.
Sustainable Growth and Innovation
Guided by planning and policies, we
will create economic opportunities to attract people and businesses to develop
and grow in a healthy manner and embrace best practices and innovative
approaches to continuously improve all of our systems and process.
Transparency, accountability and integrity
Council operates in an open,
accountable and transparent manner consistent with legislation, and respectful
of the privacy of individuals and acts and communicates in an honest, caring
and fair manner.

Recreation and Culture Service Delivery Survey
The Town of Carlyle Council has identified Recreation and Culture
as a priority in their strategic plan for the next four years. In order
to understand the usage of the town facilities and the needs/wants of the
community, we would like to gather information from the residents who live and
play in our community.
Gathering feedback is an important component to understanding your perspective as a user of recreation and culture services in Carlyle. Council has retained the services of HMC Management Inc. to lead and assist us in this information-gathering process.
We have now completed surveys with the Elementary School, the High School and the Community - see the information that we collected: Recreation & Culture Survey Results

WELCOME
The Resort Village of Chitek Lake is a small lake-side community situated in beautiful northern Saskatchewan. The less than 2 hour commute from many of Saskatchewan's major cities is well worth the drive to experience all that it has to offer; boating, fishing, quading, snowmobiling, and beaches are just a few of the fun, family-friendly activities the residents and visitors can enjoy!

pages.text:
Camping Details | chiteklake2
top of page
Resort Village of
CHITEK LAKE
rvchitek@sasktel.net
​
Chitek Lake Rec Site
We are now accepting applicants for seasonal sites for the Chitek Lake Campgrounds(Chitek Lake Recreation Site).
​
The seasonal camping rate will be $2,700 + GST per site. A total of 40 seasonal sites will be available, with returning seasonal campers given first choice of their preferred site. Applications must be received by March 29, 2027. Awarding of these sites will be through a
Draw system to be done on MARCH 31, 2027 , remaining sites will then be available for weekly reservations.
A $500 deposit check must accompany all applications. (Anyone not drawn will have their check returned). For the successful applicants the remainder of payment will be due May 1, 2027.
Sites will be available from May long weekend through until September 30th. Option will be available to leave your trailer at your site for off season storage .
To have your name added to the draw, Please forward your completed application by March 29 , 2027 to
chiteklakecampground@sasktel.net
A check for the deposit will also need to be sent to the village office in order to complete your application.
For more information you can call 1.306-984.7958
​

Chief Poundmaker Historical Centre
From Paynton: 12 km S, West to location
battle site between Militia and Chief Poundmaker’s Warriors
Interpretive Centre
walking paths and plaques
Forest Bank Church
The church was completed in 1910 by volunteers from the congregation on the southwest corner of the SE quarter of Section 14 49-24-W3. The first service on September 19, 1909 was a Harvest Festival service and regular services are still held today. The Anglican church and cemetery is located 8 miles north of Waseca and 2.5 miles east.
Fort Pitt Trail
The marker is located 12.5 miles north of Maidstone on the west side of Highway 21. The trail linked Fort Pitt and the Battleford settlements in the 1700′s. The junction of the Fort Pitt and Edmonton Trails was at Bresaylor. From Bresaylor the Fort Pitt Trail angled northwest towards the Gully Creek crossing (approximately on half mile east of Silver Lake Regional Park), then continued northwest exiting the municipality very near the northwest corner of the Tweedsmuir district. The Trail followed a very contoured course with no steep gradients.
The Trail was the service and construction route for building and maintenance of the Dominion Telegraph line, which was constructed on an almost parallel route. With the abandonment of the Dominion Telegraph in the twenties, the trail also became obsolete in favor of a surveyed road plan.
There are still traces of the Trail in the sand hill to the northeast of Maidstone. The Midwest Archaeology Society is endeavoring to preserve the remaining trail.
Pine Island
This small island, lying just off the mouth of the Gully Creek in the North Saskatchewan River, was the site of as many as five fur trading post between 1785 and 1793.
The best known trading post was Manchester House, the Hudson’s Bay Co.’s post. Fierce competition lead to fighting and ending the activity with the destruction of the forts in 1793. Although the site is inaccessible now, the view from the river banks above is breathtaking.
A huge stone and plaque were erected there in 1991 and tell the story.
To visit the site, travel north of Maidstone on Highway 21 to the Silver
Lake Regional Park road (8.5 miles). Follow this road east across the Big Gully, then follow the signs east and south.
Shiloh Baptist Church
Thirteen miles north of Maidstone on Highway 21 a sign directs you to Shiloh Church. Three miles east on that cross road and one and a half miles north will bring you to the little log church. It was built about 1912 by black settlers who emigrated from Oklahoma in 1910 and 1911 in search of a better life. Their strong faith prompted the building of this little place of worship. Perhaps it is fitting that it, alone, remains as evidence of a once prominent settlement.
Crosses mark the graves of family members who rest there beneath the huge spruce trees. The fragile little church nestles beside a dense caragana hedge and a cluster of poplars, home to hundreds of birds each summer.
Local people, realizing the importance of preserving this spot, have worked to maintain it. However, the ravages of time are winning the battle.
The church, inside and out, is as it always was, even the benches. A plaque tells the story.
Kenderdine Memorial
In 1971, the memorial to Augustus “Gus” Frederick LaFosse Kenderdine was erected top the Pikes Peak Hill near the site of the home of one of Saskatchewan’s most famous artists, teachers and promoters. He, a pioneer in the area, became the first Professor of Art at the University of Saskatchewan. In 1935, he founded the Summer School of Art at Emma Lake which attracted students from all over Canada.
Gus was an outstanding artist, well respected by his fellowmen, preserving on canvas the original beauty of our area. His paintings can be found prominently in galleries, legislative buildings and elsewhere across Canada.
Directions to the Memorial – travel 15 miles north of Maidstone on Highway 21, then 6 miles west to a bend leading down a high hill. A gate on the left will lead you up this hill to the memorial and a spectacular view, one Augustus (Gus) Kenderdine loved and painted.
Wesson Memorial
The memorial was dedicated in 1971 and was located at the site of homestead overlooking the Gully. It was moved to the Maidstone Museum grounds in 1998.
Born in 1887, in Sheffield, England, John “Jack” Henry Wesson came to Canada with this parents and siblings in 1907 and chose a homestead near Maidstone. He was very active in and for the farming community. He served on the board of the Saskatchewan Grain Growers’ Association. He became the first president of the Canadian Federation of Agriculture (1936-1940); was president of the Saskatchewan Wheat Pool from 1937 to 1960; was the president of the S.W.P. Insurance Company and the Canadian Pool Agencies Limited. He was a Wheat Pool delegate from 1924 to 1960, leading the Farmers’ March on Ottawa in both 1942 to 1959.
In 1938, he represented Canadian producers at the Empire Producers’ Conference in Australia, and was a delegate to the International Federation of Agricultural Producers’ Meetings in London and Holland, taking part in discussions leading to the World Wheat Agreement. He was advisor to the Canadian delegation to the International Wheat Agreement talks in Washington and Geneva.
He received the Commander of the British Empire in 1946. He also received an Honorary Doctorate of Laws from the University of Saskatchewan.
Jack passed away in 1965 and was buried in the Forest Bank Cemetery north west of Maidstone.

How to Book-a-Site
How to Book Online
Campsite Booking Link
Instructions for Online Reservations
Please Note: If you are having trouble with the website it could be that your personal computer firewalls and security setting are set high so it will not allow the website to process or move forward with the booking.
Please lower the security settings while making a booking then change it back to high once completed. Also, those computers that are using Windows XP and Internet Explorer 7 or lower may have trouble with the website as these systems do not update and may not be capable to handle the website. Please update your computer to Internet Explorer 8 or higher.
Click on “Book -A -Site”
Please Note: Once you start a reservations, you have 12 minutes to complete the reservation or the site will time out. During this 12 minute period the dates and site will be on hold so you can complete the process. You need to have the following information for your booking: dates you want to stay, trailer type with width and length and number of slide outs, contact information, credit card information.
Step One: First Page with the interactive map – the map shows all the sites and information about the site. In the drop down menu you will choose your type of site (15 amp, 20 amp , full service with 30 amp), then you will choose your Start Date (day you are arriving) and your End Date (day you are departing) this is in dd/mm/2016 format. You will then choose your Site Number. Scroll down to the bottom of page to Click Next. (If you are having trouble finding an available site, there may not be any availability, try leaving the site type as all, then enter start and end dates and the map and list will show all available sites for that time period).
Step Two: Trailer Information – in the dr op down menus you will choose the type of unit (motorhome, 5th wheel, etc.), you will enter the length of your trailer, the width of your trailer and the number of slide outs you have on the trailer, then you will click next on the bottom of the page.
Step Three: Guest information – the first time you make a reservation you will enter all your contact information, every other time you can login with your user name (email address) and password. Click Next on bottom of page.
Step Four: Payment Information – this is where you will enter your payment information, and billing information (if your billing information is the same as your Guest Information mark the box next to “Same as Guest’ and all your information should appear under Billing Information), enter your Payment Information including Credit Card Type (M/C, Visa), Credit Card Number, Security Code on Credit Card, Name on Credit Card. Then you Read and Accept the Terms and Conditions, Privacy Policy, Cancellation & Refund Policies and Park Rules by checking the Box and click Book – it will process and give confirmation of your booking as well as send you an email confirmation and receipt (please check your junk folder if you do not receive this email in your Inbox)
When booking a site, there is a 12 minute time limit while entering information as the site and dates are held for these 12 minutes while you are booking it.
You will pay for the site in full at the time of booking.
If there are any problems/mistakes during the booking process look for RED printing to indicate where the mistake is, or what is missing. If you have major issues, while booking please email office@lacpelletierregionalpark.ca
PLEASE NOTE THAT THE ONLY METHOD OF COMMUNICATION WILL BE BY EMAIL UNTIL THE PARK OFFICE OPENS ON APRIL 1.
To change your password, click on your name in the upper right hand side of the page and edit your information/change password
If a site will not allow reservations, could be that it is already booked, it is not available for online bookings or not available for reservations
To Make Changes/Edit a Confirmed Reservation
If you want to change your confirmed reservation, such as date of arrival, date of departure or change sites, there may be possible fees depending on when you make these changes, please see the Cancellation Policies for more information. Please follow the instructions below.
Login with your User Name and Password
The page will display all your confirmed reservations, find the reservation you want to make changes to and click on the Pencil Icon to the right of the particular reservation.
The Editing process takes you through the booking process again, so you can change the arrival or departure date with the drop down menu, on the first page, then click on Next button at the bottom of the page. This will take you to the trailer unit details if you want to change this information you can do so or you can click on the Next button at the bottom of the page.
The final page will give the details of the changes you made. It will give you the refund/payment details. You will choose a method of payment for the refund/payment, accept the Terms & Conditions then click on the Save Button to confirm your changes. This will process the refund/payment and confirm your changes.
At anytime during the editing process you can click on the Cancel button to stop making changes. This will take you back to your home page of your confirmed reservations.
To Cancel a Confirmed Reservation
If you want to cancel your confirmed reservation completely, there may be fees, depending on when you are making the changes, please see the refund policies, for more information.
Log in using your User Name and Password
This page will display all your confirmed reservations, please find the one you would like to cancel and click on the X icon to the right of the reservation you want to cancel.
This will take you directly to the final page, give you details of the refund amount, you need to choose a payment method for the refund, accept Terms & Conditions, and click on the Cancel Booking. This wil process the refund and cancel your reservation completely.
At anytime during this process, you decide you do not want to cancel your reservation, please click the Cancel button at the bottom of the page and it will take you back to the page of your confirmed reservations.

Campground
Located at 300 River Drive, at the edge of the Moose Jaw River just a few short minutes from historic downtown Moose Jaw, Lorne Calvert Campground (formerly River Park Campground) boasts 54 picturesque sites in a variety of open and shaded sites. The seasonal campground, open from May to October, is situated at the heart of Wakamow Valley and across from Kiwanis River Park Pavilion, a popular facility for family reunions and events.
Campground amenities include:
​
Picnic tables provided at campsite
Free on-site showers – NEWLY RENOVATED!!!
Flush toilets
Sewage dumping station
Firewood – $10 per load / $5 per half load
Ice available for purchase at campground office
Various outdoor games available for rent
Playground *

Campsite fees are as follows:

No Services – $30.00 per night
Electric only (30 amp/15 amp) – $39.00 per night

We do not offer a long-term or seasonal rate but we do offer a weekly rate of buy 6 nights, get the 7th night free.

Please note: When reserving a site, the first night campsite fee, Let’s Camp fee is non-refundable.
We accept cash, debit, MasterCard and Visa payments.

Melville is a small city in the east-central portion of Saskatchewan , Canada. The city is 145 kilometres (90 mi) northeast of the provincial capital of Regina and 45 kilometres (28 mi) southwest of Yorkton . Melville is bordered by the rural municipalities of Cana No. 214 and Stanley No. 215 . Its population at the 2016 census was 4,562, making it Saskatchewan's smallest city . It is also home of hockey's Melville Millionaires, who compete in the Saskatchewan Junior Hockey League , and baseball's Melville Millionaires, who competed in the Western Canadian Baseball League until 2019.

Memorial Lake Regional Park is located beside the village of Shell Lake, Saskatchewan, at the intersection of Hwy 3 and Hwy 12. We are the perfect summer destination...… golfing, camping, boating, swimming and relaxing! There is something here for everyone.
Park History
Memorial Lake was established as a regional park in 1962 by the Village of Shell Lake. The golf course was started the year before by three local men. Now we have a beautiful 18 hole grass green course, 144 campsites and 59 privately owned cabins in our park, which includes a spring fed lake, great for fishing, boating and swimming. Near the park, Memorial Hill, has a monument formed by local boy scouts in 1929. It is constructed with stones gathered from the homesteads of local men who died in WWI. There are concrete steps and handrails in place if you and your family want to venture up to visit the Cross and enjoy a beautiful view that includes the lake and forests around it. Close to the park is Shell Lake Museum, housed in an original 1930 built CNR station which exhibits artifacts and memorabilia from 1900 - 1950. A caboose sits on the track outside the museum and a log house built in 1928 is included in the area.
Age Restrictions
Campers Under the Age of 19 are not allowed to rent Campsites. ID will need to be presented upon entering the campground.
Booking Schedule 2026
January 15, 2026 - Bookings of 30 or more days
February 1 - Bookings of 1 or more days
7:00 AM on each booking day!!
50% of Fees are due upon Booking
Bookings cancelled less than 14 days in advance, there is NO refund. If cancelled more than 15 days in advance, 50% of fees paid will be refunded, minus the reservation fee and the cancellation fee. No Show Campers will be charged the full amount of booking.

Garbage & Recycling Services
Garbage Pick Up Information
The Town of Redvers has a contract with Loraas Disposal for garbage and recycling pick up for residential properties on a bi-weekly basis (Friday). All garbage should be bagged, in large trash bags. Place small grocery bags of garbage inside the large bags. Please avoid over-filling your bins. If the lid is raised, the garbage may spill on to the street upon emptying.
Please see the “Garbage Schedule” link on the website footer to access Pickup Schedule Calendars or click here for Pick Up Schedule PDF.
Commercial properties have private garbage contracts either through Loraas or another service provider.
Tree branches can be left on the boulevard, or back alley, in a neat pile for the town maintenance men to pick up on Mondays.
Recycling
CURBSIDE RECYCLING
Loraas offers curbside recycling! Recycling must be put into the containers loose. Collapse your boxes to take advantage of space inside your bin. If you have any shredded paper, please bag it in clear bags, NOT black bags.
SARCAN RECYCLING
Help keep our community clean and green by visiting the SARCAN Recycling Depot for all your recycling needs.
For more information contact 306.452.3850 Hours of Operation
Tuesday to Saturday
9:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m.

SUMMER HOURS (May 1 – October 31)
Tuesdays & Thursdays 4:00PM-7:00PM
Sundays 12:00PM-4:00PM
WINTER HOURS (November 1 – April 30)
Sundays 12:00PM-4:00PM

Happyland Campground
Happyland Campground is located along the east side of Ninette along Highway #23, and the Northern Shores of Pelican Lake.
The campground is in operation from May-September depending on weather conditions.
Stay for a night or stay for a month, you will enjoy one of our 31 fully serviced sites . Daily, weekly and monthly sites are marked and available to view on our map.
Sites are equipped with power, water, sewer, a picnic table, and a fire pit.
You will be sure to enjoy some fishing, boating, ATV riding, and walking/hiking on the trails nearby. The town of Ninette, within walking distance offers many amenities for your camping enjoyment and necessities.
Visit Let's Camp.ca to view and set up your profile and book your reservation. Happyland Campground reservations open Wednesday, April 1st, 2026 at 7:00am.
Please note: Bookings are only allowed on the Let's Camp website. No bookings will be made through the campground manager or R.M. office.
Attention: Seasonal site campers can contact the campground manager (Paul) and arrange access to their sites anytime now.
If you have questions you can contact the campground manager at (204) 523-0977 .
If you experience technical difficulties with the Let's Camp website fill out their contact form here: Contact Let's Camp .

NOTICE OF ELECTION
RURAL MUNICIPALITY OF PRAIRIE LAKES
Notice is hereby given that a vote of the RURAL MUNICIPALITY OF PRAIRIE LAKES will be taken to elect a Reeve and Councillors from the following duly nominated candidates:
For the office of Reeve:
• Cameron, Kevin
• Vallotton, Armand
For the office of Councillor, Ward 5
• Ledoyen, Shaun
• Gillingham, Andrew
• Taylor, Katherine
For the office of Councillor, Ward 2:
• Jansen, Doug
• Krushelniski, Kelly
• Beaulieu, Jacques
For the office of Councillor, Ward 6
• Durham, Rod
• Hiebert, Tim
The following duly nominated candidates are hereby declared elected by acclamation and no vote will be required:
• For the office of Councillor, Ward 1: LaBossiere, Rebecca
• For the office of Councillor, Ward 3: Cuvelier, Trent
• For the office of Councillor, Ward 4: MacKay, Michael
• For the office of Ninette LUD Committee: Treloar, Leanne and Simpson, Daniel
ELECTION DAY VOTING LOCATIONS
Voting places will be open for voting on Wednesday, October 28th, 2026, between 8:00 AM and 8:00 PM at:
Reeve, Wards 5 and 6 Belmont Drop In Centre, 117 3rd Street S, Belmont MB
Reeve, Ward 2 Ninette Community Hall, 158 Queen Street, Ninette MB
IDENTIFICATION MAY BE REQUIRED BEFORE BEING ALLOWED TO VOTE. A person may be required to produce one piece of government-issued photo identification (for example - driver’s licence or passport) or at least two other documents that provide proof of identity.
ADVANCE VOTING LOCATIONS
For the purpose of accommodating persons who are qualified to vote, but who have reason to believe that they will be absent or otherwise unable to attend the voting place on election day, an advance voting opportunity will be held:
Tuesday, October 20, 2026 between 8:00 AM and 8:00 PM
Reeve, Wards 2, 5 and 6 RM of Prairie Lakes Municipal Office, 211 3rd Street S, Belmont MB
APPLICATION TO VOTE BY SEALED ENVELOPE
A voter who is unable to go in person to the voting place on Election Day or to vote in advance may apply in person, in writing, or by email to the Senior Election Official or designate at the RM of Prairie Lakes office, 211 3rd Street S, Belmont MB R0K 0C0.
The application form is available for download from the website at rmofprairielakes.ca on the home page under Elections. You may request to vote by sealed envelope until October 25, 2026.
Dated at Brandon, Manitoba, on September 24, 2026.
Wendy Wolfe, Senior Election Official Rural Municipality of Prairie Lakes

Municipal Services - Waste Transfer Sites
There are two Waste Transfer Sites located within the Municipality.
1) Belmont Waste Transfer Site is situated on No. 23 Highway; 1 mile West of the Easterly Belmont exit road. Waste being delivered to the site is required to be sorted. All recyclables must be separated, washed with lids removed and handed to the Waste Site Supervisor/Attendant. Refrigerators/Freezers etc. may be brought to the waste transfer site where the Freon will be removed at a cost of
$25.00 .

Wednesday - 10 a.m. to 6 p.m.
Thursday - Closed

2) Dunrea Waste Transfer Site is situated on the SE 1/4 of 31-5-17 W. #101091 Head North on Road 101W, just west of Dunrea. Waste being delivered to the site is required to be sorted. Parks and Campgrounds
Lakeview Park
Located at the north end of Shoal Lake close to downtown amenities, Mounted Police Museum, and Lakeside Golf Club. There are 28 beautiful sites in total, 2 are un-serviced and 12 are seasonal lots.
The park has modern washroom/shower facilities, beach, playground, marina, and landscaped walking paths.
The park offers a playground, beach, washrooms and a boat launch.
To make a reservation, please click here
For general inquiries, please call the Campground Caretaker, ph 431-291-0354.
Shoal Lake Splash Park: Your Ultimate Summer Destination!
Looking for the perfect way to beat the summer heat and enjoy quality family time? Look no further than Shoal Lake's Splash Park! More than just a splash pad, our dynamic water playground offers a refreshing escape designed for endless fun for kids and families of all ages.
Watch smiles light up as children giggle through interactive sprayers, gentle fountains, water blasters, and many other exciting water features. But the fun doesn't stop there! Our vibrant splash pad is surrounded by convenient benches and picnic tables , perfect for parents to relax while keeping a watchful eye, or for the whole family to enjoy a packed lunch. Need a break from the sun? Take advantage of our covered gazebo or relax under the natural shade of mature trees dotted around the park.
Right next door, you'll find a fantastic playground for even more dry-land adventures, along with a beautiful beach area and swimming in Shoal Lake itself – offering a full day of aquatic enjoyment. For those who enjoy a bit of friendly competition, we also have volleyball courts . Plus, with easily accessible change rooms and washrooms , your visit will be comfortable and hassle-free.
Best of all? Admission is completely free for everyone! Come discover why Shoal Lake's Splash Park is the ideal spot for a fun-filled, refreshing, and memorable day out in our wonderful community. We can't wait to see you splash and play!
Lakeside Golf Club & Campground
Lakeside Golf Club & Campground is a community project that was built in order to provide financial support to the Lakeside Golf Course. The campground is located on the west side of the golf course, just off Highway 42.
Campground amenities include: 58 fully services sites (30x60), golf cart path along the campground, laundry room in the bathroom structure with new machines!
To book daily camping: contact the Clubhouse at 204-759-2002.
For seasonal camping contact: Scott at 204-759-3218.
Website: lakesidegolfclubandcampground.com
Check out Lakeside Golf Course Info
Marshall Chambers Park/Burlington Beach
Campground Caretaker: Tammy Campbell @ 204-764-2746 or 204-412-0101
Email: tlcampbell1@live.ca
Located at the scenic south end of Shoal Lake, 4 miles south of Shoal Lake and 1 mile west, in the cottage district. It boasts a beach, playground and fishing.
Salt Lake Carton Beach
Camping, swimming and water skiing can be enjoyed just 5 miles south of Strathclair at Carlton Beach. Carlton Beach has serviced sites, including washrooms for your camping enjoyment. Heritage Sites & Museums
Shoal Lake Mounted Police Museum
Shoal Lake is the home to one of the longest servicing police detachments in Canada and hosts Manitoba's official museum honoring the North West Mounted Police. Built in 1984 in Lakeview Park, the museum is a replica of the NWMP barracks established at the south end of Shoal Lake in 1875. It also houses the tourist information center. Open July and August. For museum information or to book a tour, please call
Christa Adriaasen - 204-573-1270.
Prairie Mountain Regional Museum
The Prairie Mountain Regional Museum is a new heritage destination being developed along the TransCanada Yellowhead Highway #16 as a joint venture between Shoal Lake and Strathclair. It displays a large collection of fully restored horse-drawn vehicles and related exhibits. The PMRM is creating a heritage rural setting to compliment the main facility and increase interpretive opportunities.
Shoal Lake Agricultural Society Fair
This is held every third Wednesday in July, catering to the entire family. Start your day with a free pancake breakfast, then go and watch our parade, then off to the fair. The heavy, light horse and cattle competitions start early and run all day. See the heavy horses pulling carts or cheer on the young equestrians. We offer an excellent hot lunch after which you can view the Home Living section featuring displays of Horticulture, Sewing, Quilting, Canning, Baking, Junior crafts & artwork & garden produce. In the area there is entertainment for both adults and children as well as inflatable structures, and a children's game corner. Outside you will find a variety of new agricultural machines for viewing as well as other activities!
Mass Grave and Monument
A monument here marks the location where, in 1899, forty five Ukrainian immigrants, forty two of them children, succumbed to scarlet fever. Most of them were buried at the site. The monument was erected in 1991 to commemorate the 100th anniversary of Ukrainian settlement in Canada. The monument is located north of Shoal Lake just off Highway #21 (North of Oakburn).
Buddas
When the Ukrainian settlers arrived in 1899, their first homes were small tent shaped pole structures covered with straw, known as buddas. Michael Swistun, who was born in a budda in 1990, later constructed two buddas on the original site next to the settlement trail and donated them with 80 acres of land to the Town of Rossburn. The Buddas are located north of Shoal Lake on PR 566.
Strathclair Museum
The Strathclair Museum situated on Main Street in Strathclair, was originally the CP Rail Station. The museum houses a myriad of the lives and times of the local pioneer. St. Georges Anglican Church and a replica blacksmith shop is also on site.

POLITIQUE SUR LA PROTECTION DES RENSEIGNEMENTS PERSONNELS

L’entreprise Chalets Camping des Sillons est soucieuse de respecter votre vie privée. Cette politique a été formulée afin de vous informer de notre engagement en matière de respect de votre vie privée et de protection de vos renseignements personnels.
En choisissant d’utiliser le site Web de Chalets Camping des Sillons pour faire votre réservation, vous acceptez l’ensemble des politiques relatives aux mesures de protection de vos renseignements personnels. Vous acceptez ainsi que Chalets Camping des Sillons recueille et utilise vos renseignements personnels conformément à la Politique, étant entendu que l’entreprise respecte la législation en vigueur en matière de renseignements personnels.
Chalets Camping des Sillons se réserve le droit de modifier la politique en tout temps et sans préavis; les changements sont en vigueur dès leur affichage sur le Site web de l’entreprise. Dans l’éventualité où vous êtes en désaccord avec la politique, vous ne pouvez pas utiliser le Site. Vous pouvez cependant exprimer votre désaccord relativement à la politique en vous adressant au responsable du Site.
​
UTILISATION DES INFORMATIONS RECUEILLIES
Chalets Camping des Sillons s’engage à préserver la confidentialité des renseignements personnels recueillis, lesquels sont notamment utilisés dans le cadre de nos activités commerciales, par exemple pour :
1. Créer votre compte client;
2. Gérer votre dossier et vous offrir les services que vous désirez obtenir;
3. Vous communiquer les informations relatives à votre réservation ou aux services que vous sollicitez;
4. Répondre à vos questions et commentaires;
5. Vous aviser des changements et nouveaux services que Chalets Camping des Sillons offre;
6. Toutes autres raisons requises par la loi et pour réaliser nos activités commerciales.
Ces renseignements sont strictement confidentiels et ne seront pas utilisés autrement que pour ce qui est prévu à la Politique. Les renseignements personnels recueillis par Chalets Camping des Sillons ne sont pas divulgués à quiconque, hormis aux représentants ou aux employés de Chalets Camping des Sillons qui ont besoin de cette information pour s’acquitter d’une tâche en fonction des éléments mentionnés dans la présente Politique.
CONSERVATION DES INFORMATIONS RECUEILLIES
Les informations sont conservées sur des serveurs sécurisés de Chalets Camping des Sillons situés au Canada. Nous observons de strictes mesures de sécurité en ce qui a trait à l’archivage et à la divulgation des informations que vous nous avez transmises, afin d’éviter tout accès non autorisé.
Même si nous prenons les mesures de sécurité convenables et requises par la loi, aucune sécurité n’est infaillible. Vous devez rester vigilants dans le traitement et la divulgation de vos renseignements personnels et éviter de transmettre des renseignements personnels par courriel non sécurisé.

The Banting Memorial Municipal Park - Town of Musgrave Harbour
Skip to main content
Menu
The Banting Memorial Municipal Park
The Banting Memorial Municipal Park is a popular camping destination in Central Newfoundland with its spectacular sandy beaches, warm atmosphere, and beautiful scenery is a must visit for anyone looking to relax, and explore the beauty that the shore has to offer.
Located just 8 km south of Musgrave Harbour along the Kittiwake Coast, on route 330 is named after Sir Frederick Banting, co-discover of insulin, who died in a plane crash just outside of Musgrave Harbour in 1941.
The park is a beautiful place for the whole family to enjoy, whether its relaxing in the sun, building castles in the sand, watching the incredible sunsets while you sit by a beach fire, taking a quiet walk around the ponds walking trail, enjoying a walk on our beautiful sandy beach, taking a swim in our fresh water pond, or the frigid Atlantic Ocean you will be sure to enjoy your stay.
The park is serviced with 30 amp 2 way, water & electrical serviced sites, and for added comfort, we have shower and washroom facilities, as well as a coin operated laundromat service, a playground for the kids with two accessible swings, and a picnic area for day visitors.
During your stay be sure to visit Banting Interpretation Center located in the park, as well as Musgrave Harbour Amusements which is an ideal spot where the family can enjoy mini golf, pedal boats, kayaks, paddle boards, a picnic area, and a variety of delicious concession foods from ice cream, sundae's, burgers, french fries, nacho's, poutine, nespresso and much much more.
